6cbcd0bf3e509341: LEA SALONGA stepped onto the stage at Dewan Filharmonik Petronas recently to warm, immediate applause. The audience clearly knew they were in the presence of a performer whose career has become a cherished part of popular culture.
Salonga boasts an extraordinary legacy. Across four decades in musical theatre, film, television, and concert halls, she has performed on Broadway and voiced two iconic Disney princesses.
The 55-year-old artiste also recently became the first Filipina to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, cementing her place in entertainment history.
A FAMILY AFFAIR ON STAGE
Yet her appearance at DFP was far more than a simple victory lap.
At its heart, the three-day show was a celebration of family, musical heritage, and the close bond between two siblings who have spent their lives surrounded by music.

Joining Salonga on stage was her younger brother, Gerard Salonga. As the resident conductor of the Malaysian Philharmonic Orchestra (MPO), Gerard led the orchestra throughout his sister's performances.
His presence added a warm, intimate touch to what could otherwise have felt like a formal retrospective. Together, the siblings turned the concert into a personal affair.
Gerard, 53, conducted the orchestral arrangements while Lea revisited the songs that marked her journey from the Philippines to the world's most prestigious stages.
JOURNEY THROUGH MUSICAL MAGIC
The concert opened with the Lea Salonga Overture, setting a tone that moved effortlessly between Disney classics, Broadway hits, and popular music.
An early highlight was the Disney Princess Medley, featuring beloved tunes such as 'Part of Your World', 'A Dream Is a Wish Your Heart Makes', 'Home', and 'Colours of the Wind'.

For Disney fans, hearing her perform 'Reflection' and 'A Whole New World' carried a magical resonance. She was, after all, the original singing voice behind Mulan and Jasmine — characters whose songs remain favourites across generations.
Her Broadway achievements received equal spotlight through selections from 'Miss Saigon', 'Les Misérables', 'Wicked', 'Company', 'Sweeney Todd', and 'Gypsy'.
The varied repertoire was a testament to her versatility, showcasing roles that require vastly different emotional approaches.

Standards like 'I Dreamed a Dream', 'Being Alive', and 'Defying Gravity' allowed Salonga to show exactly why she remains at the top of her craft: flawless vocal precision, emotional depth, and a rare ability to truly inhabit every lyric.
NOSTALGIC MOMENTS AND MEMORIES
The performance was not limited to theatrical showstoppers. Some of the most charming moments came when Salonga stepped away from musical theatre to share the music that shaped her growing up.

A lively performance of the Bee Gees' 'Stayin' Alive' was a standout delight. It led into a fond story about watching 'Saturday Night Fever' with Gerard and their mother — a sweet family memory that gave the night a personal touch.

Moments like these kept the concert lively and fresh. Instead of a rigid timeline of her achievements, the show felt like a collection of snapshots from her life, driven by her warm personality and vivid memories.
HIGH-ENERGY FINALE OF JOY
By the final stretch, the mood in the hall had shifted from quiet admiration to full celebration.
Salonga was no longer just looking back at major milestones; she was demonstrating the sheer energy of an artiste who continues to thrive across genres.

She saved one of the biggest surprises for last. Her electrifying performance of Whitney Houston's 'I Wanna Dance with Somebody' brought the audience to their feet, closing the night on a high note of pure joy rather than nostalgia.

It was a fitting finish for a concert that celebrated an extraordinary career without ever feeling stuck in the past. With Gerard conducting by her side, joined by guest singers Nigel Huckle and Sarah Galbraith alongside the MPO, the concert was a wonderful tribute to Lea Salonga's journey and the timeless joy she brings to the stage.

33ccb79a7cdf7631: SYDNEY: Asian shares slipped on Thursday as strains in sovereign bond markets were aggravated by reports some major tech companies were seeking to raise billions in debt in direct competition for limited funding.
A fresh rise in oil prices added to the pressure on Treasuries, though a strong auction of US 10-year debt overnight did help pull yields off 24-year peaks.
While lofty yields underpinned the dollar, the euro slid to near 17-month lows as concerns over France's finances spread to Italian and Greek debt.

The steady climb in borrowing costs put equities on the defensive and Japan's Nikkei eased 0.9 per cent, with South Korea down 0.6 per cent. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dipped 0.1 per cent.
On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq futures were barely changed. In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures, DAX futures and FTSE futures all edged up 0.1 per cent after sliding on Wednesday.
The Wall Street Journal added to media reports that SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle were looking to raise money to buy AI chips.

Broadcom was looking for US$50 billion in financing, while SpaceX was planning to issue US$30 billion in investment-grade debt and raise US$10 billion in loans to buy chips from Nvidia, which is a major shareholder in SpaceX.
The news saw credit default insurance on SpaceX jump to record highs, while its shares and bonds lost ground.

Nigel Green, CEO of deVere Group, warned of a dangerous loop where Nvidia was bankrolling the very customers who buy its products, leaving global investors at risk if the expected profits failed to materialise.
"The AI build out started on cash," said Green. "It's increasingly running on credit, and credit changes the risk profile entirely."
"Debt has to be repaid on schedule, whether the revenues show up or not," he added. "And this debt is landing in the bond funds and pension pots of savers right around the world."
**SOVEREIGN BONDS VS CORPORATE DEBT**
Still, the fact much of this money will be spent on AI equipment could be positive for earnings in the semiconductor and memory sectors.
Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected a 783 per cent jump in third-quarter operating profit to 107.4 trillion won (US$80.17 billion), though its shares eased 0.3 per cent.
All this corporate debt is coming at a time when sovereign bond markets are being sorely tested by inflation fears, ever-widening budget deficits and rising cash rates.
Minutes of the Federal Reserve's last meeting released on Wednesday showed "most" members considered another rate hike likely by year end, though they would approach each meeting with an open mind.
Markets imply just a 19 per cent chance the Fed will move again this month, but are 80 per cent priced for a rise in December.
"We expect a second Fed hike in December, though we see a strong chance the Fed ultimately concludes further tightening is unnecessary," wrote analysts at Goldman Sachs in a note.
The prospect of a pause in tightening helped keep 2-year Treasury yields at 4.78 per cent, while 10-year yields nudged up to 5.298 per cent having hit a 24-year top of 5.326 per cent overnight.

Strains in the French bond market led Bank of France head Emmanuel Moulin to acknowledge the country's economic situation was serious, but he reassured investors it did not need help from the European Central Bank.
Investors reacted by dumping the euro, which was pinned at US$1.1198 having lost 0.6 per cent overnight. A break of the recent low at US$1.1161 would risk a retreat to US$1.1065.

The dollar was the main beneficiary of the single currency's woes and its index rose to 102.22, near an 18-month peak. It was off 0.1 per cent on the yen at 157.90, with the Japanese currency protected by the threat of intervention.
In commodity markets, Brent futures rose 0.9 per cent to US$101.14 a barrel, while US crude futures added 0.8 per cent to US$89.02 a barrel.
Non-interest-bearing gold has suffered as yields climbed, leaving it at US$4,105 an ounce and near two-month lows.

11fb87c74f6b27b9: KUCHING: The Sarawak state legislative assembly is expected to be dissolved in November or two weeks after the state's Budget 2027 is passed.

4bb51ff21b7f27ea: VATICAN CITY, Oct 8 — Pope Leo XIV on Wednesday called on the Roman Catholic Church to revise the way it helps families and handles failed marriages as he opened a major weeklong religious assembly.

With the church debating how it recognises separations, Leo did not directly mention divorce but called on Catholic leaders to reflect on the “experience of fragility” and the handling of “situations marked by limitations, wounds, and apparent failures.”

Leo’s predecessor, Francis, who died in 2025, made a tentative step in 2016 for Catholics who have divorced and remarried in civil ceremonies to receive Communion. It sparked a Church-wide debate and pushback from conservative Catholics. Leo’s address was made to a week-long closed assembly of bishops from 120 countries, who will be joined by leaders from Eastern churches, experts, theologians and 11 lay couples to mark the 10th anniversary of the late Pope Francis’ “Amoris Laetitia” (The Joy of Love) document.
According to Church teaching, a Catholic who divorces and then remarries in a civil ceremony remains bound by the first marriage, unless it was officially annulled, and cannot receive communion.
“Amoris Laetitia” introduced the possibility of case-by-case decisions, without challenging the principle that a Catholic marriage cannot be dissolved.
Leo said: “Young people continue to aspire to love, fidelity, and a sense of belonging, but many struggle to envision how such a vision of love can take shape in their own lives.”
“In many contexts, a gap has widened between the way sexuality and intimacy are experienced and the Christian vision of marriage,” he said.
The assembly, which is to release a final report, is to discuss marriage and difficulties faced in life and could look at ways to welcome the LGBTQ community, another one of Francis’ concerns. — AFP
74607ced71ad631d: SEOUL: Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected its quarterly profit would top 100 trillion won, a world first for a technology company, estimating a nearly nine-fold jump in third-quarter earnings as booming demand for AI chips drove strong memory sales.

The world's largest memory chipmaker estimated an operating profit of 107.4 trillion won (US$80.17 billion) for the July-September period, slightly ahead of an LSEG SmartEstimate of 106.1 trillion won, a regulatory filing showed.

The forecast marks Samsung's fourth straight quarter of record operating profit, underscoring a deepening global memory chip shortage as AI infrastructure investment outpaces supply growth, which has driven chip prices up sharply.
Samsung and Micron expect the imbalance to persist into 2028, although rising costs, Chinese competition and potential US semiconductor tariffs pose risks to the longer-term earnings outlook.
"There were uncertainties surrounding Samsung's earnings as analysts cut their estimates, but the results turned out to be better than expected," said Lee Jae-won, an analyst at Yuanta Securities.
Lee said investors would also be closely watching for details of Samsung's shareholder return policy during its earnings call later this month.

Prices have soared due to the tight supply of conventional DRAM and NAND chips as well as growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), essential for processing vast amounts of data for AI applications.
Third-quarter revenue would likely rise 127 per cent to 195 trillion won from a year earlier, Samsung said.
The company will release detailed results, including a breakdown of earnings by business division, on October 29.
Samsung's shares rose 0.3 per cent in early trade, outperforming a 0.1 per cent fall in the benchmark KOSPI.
AI MEMORY BOOM DRIVES EARNINGS

Memory chips are expected to account for the bulk of the earnings improvement. Analysts expect supply to continue to lag demand, with the imbalance potentially widening in 2027 as AI-related demand absorbs an increasing share of global memory capacity.

Against that backdrop, conventional DRAM bit shipments are expected to remain broadly flat because of limited inventories, while HBM shipments could rise sharply from the previous quarter on strong demand for HBM4, analysts said.
Douglas Kim of Douglas Research Advisory estimated that Samsung's HBM bit shipments expanded by close to 50 per cent quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter.

US rival Micron, a key supplier of high-bandwidth memory to Nvidia, said the chip market could be tighter in 2027 and 2028 than this year, after forecasting quarterly revenue well above estimates on Wednesday.
A stronger South Korean won may offset some of the gains by reducing the value of dollar-denominated overseas sales when converted into local currency.

The memory chip boom also presents a challenge for Samsung's other businesses, particularly its smartphone and consumer electronics divisions, which face mounting pressure from higher component costs.
Higher memory prices, while benefiting Samsung's semiconductor arm, are raising costs for its own smartphones and other electronic devices, squeezing margins in those businesses.
Meanwhile, Samsung's contract chipmaking, or foundry, business is expected to remain loss-making because of the burden of fixed costs and still-low utilisation rates, analysts said.

However, utilisation is expected to improve over the next several quarters, supported by stronger demand for advanced manufacturing processes. Samsung has been seeking to narrow the gap with industry leader TSMC in advanced contract chip manufacturing.

In a potential boost to its foundry ambitions, AMD chief executive officer Lisa Su said on Wednesday that the US chipmaker continues to explore partnership opportunities with Samsung in the memory and foundry businesses.
CHINESE COMPETITION, US TARIFFS CLOUD OUTLOOK
Despite the favourable supply backdrop for Samsung and other memory makers, the longer-term expansion of Chinese memory-chip makers remains a potential challenge.
For now, Chinese memory makers are also expected to remain more dependent on domestic customers, including Chinese AI-chip developers and PC and smartphone manufacturers.
Analysts said, however, US restrictions on China's access to advanced chipmaking equipment continue to limit how quickly Chinese producers can expand.
Another uncertainty is the prospect of US semiconductor tariffs, as Washington pushes chipmakers to expand manufacturing capacity in the US.

However, analysts said it would take several years for new US chip manufacturing capacity to boost global memory supply, as large-scale chip fabrication plants take years to build and ramp up production.

26f93c1e277e88c7: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 8 — Microsoft is pushing a “hybrid intelligence” future with a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips and will cost more than US$2,500 (RM10,200), the company announced Wednesday.

The launch is part of a broader push by tech companies to release hardware that can handle more AI computing on-device and offline, so users don’t have to rely solely on remote cloud data centres, where running AI is slower and more expensive.
It also sees Nvidia, whose data centre processors power the AI revolution, make a move into personal computing, a sector dominated for decades by chips from Intel and Qualcomm.

“The trajectory for me is so clear. There will never be a moment where we will go and look and say: ‘Oh, this runs locally, this runs in the cloud.’ You will expect this hybrid intelligence to be everywhere and pervasive,” CEO Satya Nadella said during an event in San Francisco.
He was joined onstage by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who echoed the idea that AI will be integrated into all computing going forward and on all devices.
Agentic AI, in particular, will be central to software development, Huang said, referring to systems programmed to be autonomous and perform tasks without supervision.
With all the changes from AI, “the computer has to be revolutionized,” Huang said.
The partnership between the two US-based tech titans helps them compete with Apple, Intel and AMD in the personal computing market.
Apple unveiled two desktop computers in September, the Mac mini and Mac Studio, which it touted as powerful new options capable of processing AI software locally.
Microsoft has been working on building “AI PCs” since at least 2024, when its laptops were powered by Qualcomm chips.
The new Surface Ultra will use Nvidia’s state-of-the-art AI chip, RTX Spark, which the semiconductor giant announced earlier this year.
It will cost US$2,599 and begins shipping on October 16.
Some AI computing power and data will be processed locally, or on the device, while other applications are still handled remotely via Microsoft’s cloud computing services.
“We built it for developers and creators pushing the limits of performance,” Microsoft Executive Vice President of Windows and Device Pavan Davuluri said on Wednesday.

The news comes just a couple of weeks after Microsoft announced it would integrate Word, Excel and Powerpoint into its AI-powered assistant Copilot, in an effort to make AI the entry point for its famous suite of productivity software.
OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, and Claude-maker Anthropic each launched their own document creation tools in recent months.
The two San Francisco-based AI labs are also key suppliers for Microsoft, since Copilot runs primarily on their models.
Microsoft’s in-house models currently only power a few products, such as GitHub’s Copilot coding tool.
In June, Microsoft also unveiled its own cutting-edge artificial intelligence models – a crucial step toward reducing its dependence on OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT.
Microsoft, the first company to have invested massively in OpenAI, has for several years been seeking to reduce its reliance on its Sam Altman-led partner.
It renegotiated their alliance last year and retains only a non-exclusive license on its technology until 2032 though is OpenAI’s biggest shareholder. — AFP
ebd9e1c344515dd0: SINGAPORE: The dollar held near its strongest level in a year-and-a-half in subdued trading at the start of the Asian session on Thursday, after hawkish minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) signalled policymakers at the US central bank viewed inflation as the biggest risk to their outlook.
The dollar index, which measures its strength against a basket of six currencies, was steady at 102.23 after rising 0.3 per cent on Wednesday.
The greenback remains within a few pips of its strongest levels since April 9, 2025, following the market turmoil that accompanied the so-called Liberation Day tariff announcement the previous week.

Federal Reserve policymakers voted unanimously to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point at the US central bank's September 15-16 meeting, but minutes released Wednesday indicated divisions over their rationale for doing so.

"The FOMC's minutes reinforced the hawkish tone accompanying the Fed's September rate hike, with most participants still viewing further tightening as appropriate and almost all seeing inflation risks tilted to the upside at the time of the meeting," Westpac analysts wrote.
The minutes did little to shift expectations that the Fed will refrain from hiking at its meeting later this month.

Fed funds futures are pricing an implied 19 per cent probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's next two-day meeting ending Oct 28, unchanged from a day earlier, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Against the yen, the US dollar was down 0.2 per cent at 157.815 yen after data released on Thursday showed Japan's current account surplus stood at 4.062 trillion yen (US$25.7 billion) in August, higher than economists' median forecast for a surplus of 3.19 trillion yen.
The Australian dollar and its kiwi counterpart were both flat at US$0.6960 and US$0.5600 respectively.
Against the Chinese yuan, the US dollar was flat at 6.7015 yuan in offshore trade.
The euro was flat at US$1.1201, while the British pound was also unchanged at US$1.3215.
Bitcoin slipped 0.2 per cent to US$83,233.40 while ether nudged 0.1 per cent lower to US$2,571.07.
b92049ad175fedb2: KUALA LUMPUR: Development expenditure is projected to rise a modest 3.8 per cent year-on-year to RM83 billion under Malaysia's 2027 Budget, CIMB Securities said.
The government allocated RM80 billion for development expenditure in 2026 Budget.

An estimated RM9 billion decline in petrol and diesel subsidies to RM32 billion in 2027 could provide fiscal headroom to fund development projects, CIMB Securities analysts Kenny Mak Hoy Ken and Wei Yi Tan said in a report today.

In the first nine months of 2026, domestic project awards reached RM177 billion, equivalent to 76 per cent and 72 per cent of the total value of jobs awarded in 2024 (RM234 billion) and 2025 (RM244 billion), respectively.
"Public-funded projects, however, amounted to only RM37 billion, or 57 per cent and 63 per cent of the levels recorded in 2024 and 2025, respectively.

"Beyond the higher headline development expenditure projections for 2027, we prefer to focus on project awards and execution, as certain allocations may relate to the balance of ongoing jobs rather than new tenders," the analysts said.
The timing of project awards could also be brought forward ahead of the 16th general election, which must be called by February 2028, they said.

The report expects most infrastructure spending under 2027 Budget to be channelled towards small- to mid-sized projects, with a continued focus on narrowing development gaps by directing more allocations to East Malaysia, particularly Sabah and Sarawak, as well as other interior areas.
"Consequently, in our view, key areas of focus would include water infrastructure and pipe replacements, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure and grid investments," the analysts said.

Potential big-ticket infrastructure tenders under 2027 Budget include the second phases of the Rasau and Langat 2 water supply schemes, Civil Main Contract 3 (CMC 3) of the Penang Mutiara Line LRT, the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme, and new road and utility projects in Sabah and Sarawak, the report said.

a99332b29b18e5ad: KUALA LUMPUR: Victims of domestic violence can obtain an Emergency Protection Order (EPO) from the Welfare Department without first lodging a police report, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said.

She said the EPO was one of three forms of legal protection available to victims, alongside the Interim Protection Order (IPO) and Protection Order (PO), which are issued by the courts and require a police report.
"The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry emphasises four key approaches to addressing domestic violence: prevention, protection, intervention and rehabilitation.

"To strengthen the family institution, our programmes emphasise prevention. Subsequently, when an incident occurs, we focus on protection. We must have intervention measures in place, and another vital aspect is rehabilitation," she said during the 'Kasih Lensa Keluarga' podcast titled 'With Love, Violence Ends!' (Dengan Kasih, Keganasan Terhenti!), which was broadcast live on Bernama TV yesterday.
Lim said rehabilitation was essential to ensure victims who had escaped domestic violence could rebuild their lives and become self-reliant.
She said domestic violence was not the way to resolve family conflicts. Instead, issues should be addressed through communication, mutual respect and open discussion.
"If violence or a threat to safety occurs, victims must seek help," she said.

Meanwhile, Lim said the ministry was collaborating with the police, government agencies, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the community to address the issue through a committee focused on data, education, capacity building and protection.
She said the community, including families and neighbours, must also play a role.

"Neighbours and family members need to shift their mindset and realise that this is not a matter of interfering in other people's family affairs. Domestic violence is a crime; therefore, we can lodge a report," she said.
The 24-hour Talian Kasih 15999 hotline serves as a channel for the public to lodge reports and seek advice and psychosocial counselling services, with complaints referred to the Welfare Department.
93fcb6607da4da23: KUALA LUMPUR Oct 8 — We ordered not one, but two plates of the duck egg char kway teow at Next Gen Kopitiam in Maluri, Cheras.
Now, this isn’t because we were regulars who had tasted these noodles many times before; we were, in fact, first time visitors.
Why then the vote of confidence?
If anything, I have learned to trust the recommendations of my friends. One of whom worked nearby and tells me how she’d drop by Next Gen Kopitiam for her char kway teow fix.
That’s good enough for me.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Next Gen Kopitiam in Maluri, Cheras. — Picture by CK Lim

Though, when we first arrived, having walked a few minutes from the nearby MRT station (parking is, quite frankly, horrendous in this area; public transport will keep you sane), and saw the shop had an air-conditioned area, I couldn’t quite but wonder if my friend’s loyalty is due more to the comfort than the char of the kway teow.
But I have learned to have faith in my friends till proven wrong (and I rarely am).
The char kway teow stall owner, Uncle Wong, runs it alone which is admirable considering how most other stalls at the kopitiam hire helpers.
Back inside (yes, like my friend, we opted for air-conditioned seating inside the shop), our orders of coffee and toast soon arrived.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Rich and ‘kaw’ salted ‘cham’. — Picture by CK Lim
First, our requisite cups of cham, one hot and one iced: these are rich and kaw, every sip intense and robust.
We checked with each other and agreed that the local coffee was salted, which hits the spot especially with the iced version.
The shop offers the typical range of roti bakar, including the redoubtable butter and kaya, but their signature is a salted egg yolk version called the Golden Toast.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The shop’s signature Golden Toast. — Picture by CK Lim
Sounds gimmicky, or at least that’s what we thought at first. The appearance wasn’t the most impressive either; the salted egg yolk topping resembles a monotonous layer of mentaiko.
Looks can be deceiving, of course. Rather than entirely salty, the creamy topping is closer to salty-sweet, which parallels and pairs well with the salted cham.
The crust is lightly toasted but tear into the bread and you’ll realise the crumb is almost steamed, perhaps thanks to the impermeable layer of salted egg yolk cream.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Liquid manna: half boiled eggs. — Picture by CK Lim
Toasted and fluffy? Now this is a textural contrast we relish.
Have this alone or dipped into the luxurious cham or liquid manna in the form of half boiled eggs.
Time for our “main course” — our duck egg char kway teow. Uncle Wong fries each plate of char kway teow individually so they might arrive separately but you’re assured of freshness, so to speak.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Uncle Wong fries each plate of ‘char kway teow’ individually. — Picture by CK Lim
I usually prefer a “dryer” style of char kway teow; Uncle Wong’s version does look wetter than your typical char kway teow.
However, it is still full of wok hei and every strand benefits from both char and a bite that is more tender.
More marvellous than too moist, if you get my meaning.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Wetter than your typical ‘char kway teow’ but still full of ‘wok hei’. — Picture by CK Lim
Yet another reason to keep following the advice and recommendations of my friends; I am convinced they are even bigger gluttons than I am (and that’s high praise indeed!).
Next Gen Kopitiam 新时代茶餐厅
91, Jalan Jejaka 2,
Maluri, Cheras,
KL.

cea31947e826ed0d: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Thursday as markets awaited the tabling of 2027 Budget for clues on the direction of the country's fiscal deficit.
At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0845/0895 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0850/0895.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit edged higher despite a stronger US dollar following the release of minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which lifted the US Dollar Index (DXY) 0.40 per cent to 102.242 points.

"The ringgit remains range-bound as markets await 2027 Budget for clues on the fiscal deficit, particularly amid energy price shocks that are expected to affect the 3.5 per cent of gross domestic product target for 2026," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded mostly lower against major currencies at the opening.

3eba967a2ee207de: SENCUR, Slovenia: Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar was missing, but Slovenia still had a home hero to celebrate as Primoz Roglic won the European Championships time-trial title on Wednesday.

The Tokyo 2020 Olympic time-trial champion started fast and held off his charging challengers to capture the crown by 6.59 seconds ahead of Frenchman Bruno Armirail, whose compatriot Maxime Decomble finished third.

Roglic, 36, benefited from the absence of world and Olympic time-trial champion Remco Evenepoel and Italian specialist Filippo Ganna as he was cheered on by local fans along the 22-kilometre course in Sencur.

"It's simply a great feeling. Of course, it's my victory, but it's also for all the people along the course and everyone who made it possible for the European Championships to take place in Slovenia," said Roglic.

With French prodigy Paul Seixas skipping the European meet to focus on this weekend's final Monument one-day classic — the Tour of Lombardy — none of the medalists from the world championships just over two weeks ago featured on the start line.
In the women's event, world champion Marlen Reusser continued her dominance in the discipline by securing the European title for the fifth consecutive year.
Dutch rider Demi Vollering, who won the world and European road race titles over the previous 10 days, finished second, while Juliette Berthet of France took third. – AFP
f1aa1dfdc0d3381d: Umum mengetahui istilah 3R merujuk kepada isu, kes atau sebarang perbincangan semberono yang dilabel sensitif kerana ia melibatkan perihal 'Religion' (Agama), 'Race' (Kaum), dan 'Royalty' (Raja/Institusi Diraja). Saya menggunakan istilah semberono kerana selalunya wacana di dalam ruang akademik mengenai 3R ini amat berhemah, ilmiah dan terguna pakai untuk mereka yang ahli. Akan tetapi ia berbeza apabila memasuki ruang awam, iaitu apabila 3R tiba di lidah, atau jari-jemari netizen.

Adalah menjadi kebiasaan untuk pihak berkuasa seperti polis dan Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) memberi perhatian berat, dan selalunya memantau secara mendalam sebarang hantaran atau perbincangan mengenai 3R di pelbagai platform media sosial. Tugasan ini tentulah melelahkan dan membuang masa. Malangnya inilah realiti hari ini. Tujuan pemerhatian serius ini agak jelas; ia demi mengekang sebarang provokasi, fitnah, mahupun ucapan berbaur kebencian yang boleh menggugat perpaduan dan ketenteraman awam. Kes-kes 3R lazimnya disiasat di bawah Akta Hasutan, Kanun Keseksaan, atau Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia.

Ada banyak contoh mengenai R pertama, iaitu agama; mungkin yang paling terkini adalah satu ucapan oleh Noorazli Said, ketua Umno sebuah bahagian, yang didakwa mempersendakan paderi dan biarawati Katolik dengan 'jenaka' berunsur seksual semasa Perhimpunan Agung Umno (PAU) 2026 baru-baru ini.

Ekoran dari ucapan menjijikkan itu, pelbagai pihak termasuk pemimpin Sabah, Persatuan Gereja Sarawak (ACS), dan Wanita PKR mengecam 'jenaka' tersebut sebagai tidak menghormati agama. Malangnya 'jenaka' itu tidak berseni dan tidak boleh pula dihujahkan sebagai suatu satira. Meskipun Noorazli memohon maaf secara terbuka atas kecalaran hati dan ketergurisan jiwa serta salah faham yang timbul; 'jenaka' atau ucapan beliau itu telah merebak dan dikongsi secara meluas lantas menyakitkan hati penganut Kristian Katolik.

Manakala untuk R kedua, iaitu kaum, serba sedikit ia masih berkait dengan identiti agama. Ini kerana di Malaysia, kategorisasi agama selalu dihubungkan dengan bangsa tertentu. Pada tahun 2024 misalnya, dalam satu kes yang turut berkait dengan agama, Ahli-ahli Parlimen berbangsa India menggesa Kementerian Dalam Negeri mengambil tindakan tegas kepada penceramah berbangsa India yang telah memeluk Islam, Muhammad Zamri Vinoth Kalimuthu dan pihak-pihak lain yang didakwa menghina agama Hindu. Mereka juga mendakwa tindakan terhadap 3R yang melibatkan kaum bukan Melayu dan agama bukan Islam selalunya agak perlahan ditangani.
R, ketiga adalah institusi diraja yang mana khusus untuk mereka yang melakukan penghinaan terhadap Yang di-Pertuan Agong dan raja-raja Melayu.

Sebagai misalan, dalam satu perkembangan berkait isu yang melibatkan kedudukan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir; tokoh politik dari Wawasan dan bekas menteri besar Negeri Sembilan, Rais Yatim didakwa mengikut Seksyen 4(1)(b) Akta Hasutan yang boleh dihukum di bawah Subseksyen 4(1) akta sama. Sabit kesalahan membawa hukuman denda tidak melebihi RM5,000 atau penjara tidak lebih tiga tahun atau kedua-duanya.

Seperti disebut awal, terdapat tanggapan pendakwaan melibatkan isu 3R kadang-kala agak berat sebelah. Meskipun dakwaan 3R boleh menimpa sesiapa pun, tidak dapat dinafikan golongan kanan dan konservatif Melayu sering menggunakan naratif 3R sebagai instrumen untuk mengukuhkan jati diri, mempertahankan status quo, dan menuntut hak-hak yang mereka percaya, sedang 'diancam' atau 'terancam'. Seringnya hujah mereka adalah 3R teras kelangsungan hidup bangsa Melayu.

Dalam hal institusi diraja, golongan kanan Melayu misalnya berpegang yang institusi diraja bukan sekadar simbol perlembagaan, tetapi penjaga dan pelindung langsung kepada hak orang Melayu dan kesucian agama Islam. 3R akan dihujahkan untuk melabel golongan progresif atau bukan Melayu sebagai 'kurang ajar' atau 'derhaka' sekiranya mereka mempersoalkan sebarang titah atau peranan institusi diraja. Ini bererti golongan konservatif boleh secara taktikal berselindung di sebalik hujah institusi diraja untuk beroleh legitimasi moral yang konon perjuangan mereka itu direstui oleh 'payung negara'.

Oleh sebab isu 3R adalah ayam gepuk atau ayam geprek untuk masyarakat Melayu yang kian konservatif, parti politik tertentu akan tanpa segan silu menunggang naratif 3R untuk memperlihatkan diri mereka sebagai pejuang hak konservatif.

Namun demikian, dalam hal di Negeri Sembilan, tindakan terhadap penentang-penentang Tuanku Muhriz dapat dikatakan sangat perlahan. Seingat saya sudah dua kali Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) menggunakan istilah penderhaka buat kelompok 'dago dagi' (derhaka dalam Adat Perpatih) dan terbaru pada 4 Oktober 2026, Dewan ini "memohon supaya pihak-pihak penguatkuasa terutamanya polis dan Jabatan Peguam Negara mengambil langkah-langkah yang sewajarnya untuk menyiasat dan memulakan pendakwaan atas kesalahan-kesalahan jenayah yang telah mereka lakukan melalui tindakan-tindakan seperti yang telah dinyatakan di atas". Menurut Dewan, "ini penting supaya mereka tidak secara terus mengambil tindakan-tindakan dan membuat kenyataan-kenyataan yang bertentangan dengan perlembagaan dan undang-undang yang akan mengelirukan pentadbiran negeri dan rakyat jelata".

Meskipun seruan DKU ini ternyata keras dan tegas iaitu agar tindakan segera diambil terhadap kelompok yang mempertikaikan keabsahan Tuanku Muhriz, pihak berkuasa ternyata sangat berhati-hati. Ramai yang percaya, tindakan penuh waspada pihak berkuasa ini kerana sistem diraja di Negeri Sembilan agak unik dan berbeza dari negeri lain.

Sungguhpun begitu, saya mempunyai pandangan berbeza. Memang mulanya perbahasan mengenai kedudukan Yamtuan Besar dan Undang itu terhad kepada pertikaian tafsiran adat. Akan tetapi sejak akhir-akhir ini sembang isu adat dikuasai oleh lasykar siber, dan lasykar siber ada tuannya. Selalunya tuan lasykar siber adalah jembalang tertentu yang berhalimunan.

Jika di alam nyata, ramai individu tidak akan berani mengeluarkan kenyataan berbaur perkauman atau menghina institusi diraja lantaran risiko sosial dan undang-undang yang jelas. Namun demikian di dalam talian, pengguna Threads misalnya boleh menyembunyikan identiti sebenar mereka di sebalik nama samaran atau profil palsu. Ada banyak akaun meragukan tanpa identiti sempurna. Mereka adalah cybertrooper berbayar. Oleh sebab mereka tidak perlu punya nama sebenar, ia memberikan rasa selamat untuk mereka bertindak agresif, memaki hamun, serta menyebarkan kebencian terhadap Yamtuan Besar tanpa memikirkan akibatnya. Hujung-hujung mereka keseronokan mendapat bayaran lebat.

Kelengahan dan kelenguhan pihak berkuasa bertindak sehingga memaksa institusi diraja Negeri Sembilan mengeluh lebih dari sekali mengenai penderhaka-penderhaka ini sebetulnya agak mencengangkan. Ia seolah-olah mereka yang melakukannya memiliki perlindungan, dan berasa kebal. Seolah-olah ada 'jembalang besar' yang merestui perbuatan mereka.

Lebih memburukkan keadaan adalah ruang digital juga mengalami budaya kongsi dahulu atau gejala 'information velocity' di mana pengguna berkongsi maklumat serta-merta tanpa perlu sebarang pengesahan. Dalam tindakan refleks, jari kita akan mudah untuk 'repost', 'retweet' atau menekan butang 'like' dan emoji. Hantaran teks, video potongan pendek, atau tangkapan layar yang dimanipulasi sering disebarkan dalam kumpulan WhatsApp keluarga atau kerjiranan tanpa perlu menyemak kesahihan. Semua ini berpotensi pula mengakibatkan ahli kumpulan bertingkah, membusut menjadi telingkah dan lama-kelamaan membukit menjadi gaduh dan kelahi.

Perlu diingat pendekatan lasykar siber dalam apa jua keadaan adalah mencipta persepsi dengan naratif sebelah pihak. Ini kerana lasykar ini adalah 'askar upahan' para politikus di medan siber. Mereka berperanan untuk mencipta atau menonokkan pandangan awam. Dengan memomokkan fakta palsu mengenai Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan seperti Tuanku Muhriz kononnya cenderung kepada DAP, atau menggadai tanah adat; mereka yang melakukan hantaran begini berharap dapat mencederakan imej seorang raja yang kelihatannya begitu bersabar mendepani perangai dan tingkah laku pengkritik.

Sebenarnya Tuanku Muhriz tidak akan kudung atau puntung meski diserang bertalu-talu oleh lasykar siber. Tembaklah banyak mana pun. Memang Tuanku Muhriz tidak akan membalas pencaci hidup-hidup. Memang lasykar siber pula tidak pun sedikit rasa bersalah membuatkan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud menitiskan air mata sebak dan terharu di KLIA sepulangnya dari bercuti.

Namun, sebagai pengkaji orang Melayu dari Institut Alam dan Tamadun Melayu, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, saya ingin membawa perhatian bahawa dalam kepercayaan orang Melayu; status seorang raja yang sah jurai keturunannya tidak akan terjejas. Mereka yang dakwa-dakwi raja itu yang selalunya akan terpelanting, dan hancur binasa.

Sebetulnya seruan DKU agar penderhakaan dibendung amatlah penting untuk segera ditunaikan. Gejala '3R' di Negeri Sembilan ini akan mewabak. Sudah ada beberapa akaun media sosial yang hidup kemudian tiba-tiba mati; atau mendadak timbul, kemudian gesit tenggelam; khusus dalam mempertikaikan sistem pemilihan atau penggiliran sultan atau raja di negeri lain.
Waktu itu kelak, gejala ini akan lebih sukar ditangani.

95213f6094ab797c: Germany's Daniel Altmaier rallied for a 1-6, 7-6 (5), 6-4 victory against Denmark's Holger Rune in first-round action Wednesday at the Rolex Shanghai Masters.

Altmaier trailed 4-3 in the deciding set before sweeping the last three games, two on his own serve, to finish in 2 hours and 15 minutes. He converted his only break point of the match in the ninth game to take the lead.

"There were a couple of points where I really had to fight," Altmaier said, pointing out his spectacular backhand pass to set up match point. "I've been working on that the past few days. My confidence hasn't been the highest. It paid off in a really special moment today."
Rune, who returned to competition last month after rupturing his Achilles last October, had more winners (34 to 29) and fewer unforced errors (29 to 31).
Altmaier's opponent in the second round of the ATP 1000 tournament will be World No. 4 and No. 3 seed Ben Shelton. Altmaier won their only previous meeting earlier this year on clay in Hamburg.
Fellow German Yannick Hanfmann also advanced with a marathon 6-7 (4), 7-6 (3), 7-6 (7) win against Poland's Kamil Majchrzak in 3 hours and 13 minutes.

Three Frenchmen moved on, with Arthur Gea rallying for a 6-7 (3), 6-1, 6-2 win against Portugal's Jaime Faria and Quentin Halys ousting Hong Kong's Coleman Wong 6-4, 7-6 (5). Adrian Mannarino was leading 6-3, 2-2 when Georgia's Nikoloz Basilashvili had to retire.

Wednesday's other winners included a pair of wild-card entries from China. Yibing Wu defeated Michael Zheng 6-3, 7-6 (6) and Yi Zhou outlasted Italian qualifier Mattia Bellucci 6-4, 3-6, 7-6 (4) in 2 hours and 45 minutes.
Wu will face No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev of Germany in the second round.

Italy's Matteo Berrettini posted a 6-7 (3), 6-1, 6-4 comeback victory against Aleksander Kovacevic. Slovakia's Alex Molcan also went the distance for a 4-6, 6-1, 6-2 win over Italy's Federico Cina.

Four others advanced in straight sets. Britain's Arthur Fery defeated Croatia's Marin Cilic 7-6 (2), 6-1; Serbia's Miomir Kecmanovic beat Japan's Sho Shimabukuro 6-2, 6-4; Russia's Roman Safiullin earned a 7-5, 6-3 win over Australia's Rinky Hijikata; and Japan's Rei Sakamoto ousted Argentina's Marco Trungelliti 6-3, 7-5.
a15aa74163e85f87: KUALA LUMPUR: The World Bank has raised its 2026 growth forecast for Malaysia to 5.1 per cent but warned that a potential reversal in the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom could pose a key downside risk to the economy.

The upward revision of 0.7 percentage points from its previous projection reflects stronger-than-expected economic activity in the first half of the year, with domestic demand expected to remain the main driver of growth.
Economists said Malaysia should leverage the current AI investment boom to strengthen capabilities that can support the economy even if global AI activity slows.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia associate professor of property economics Dr Muhammad Najib Razali told Business Times that the country should prioritise moving up the semiconductor value chain.
He said this should include areas such as advanced packaging, chip design, research and development (R&D), specialised technologies and homegrown intellectual property.
"Malaysia should also focus less on the headline value of data-centre investments and more on domestic value creation.
"Important measures should include Malaysian supplier participation, skilled employment, technology transfer, R&D, intellectual property and productivity improvements.
"At the same time, Malaysia should accelerate AI adoption among domestic companies, particularly small and medium enterprises.

"The key question should gradually shift from 'How much AI investment are we attracting?' to 'How much productivity are Malaysian businesses generating from AI?' Education policy must support this transition," he said.
Najib said Malaysia could draw lessons from Singapore's approach to developing AI-ready talent and South Korea's focus on integrating AI into industrial development.

He said Malaysia should adopt a combination of both approaches, with universities and technical and vocational education and training institutions embedding AI across disciplines to equip graduates with both professional expertise and AI skills.
"Ultimately, Malaysia should not aim to become dependent on the AI boom. It should aim to become AI-enabled.

"The real measure of success is not simply the number of data centres or billions of ringgit invested, but how much Malaysian intellectual property, skilled employment, domestic business participation and productivity are created from those investments," Najib said.
MALAYSIA EXPOSED TO AI SLOWDOWN
World Bank lead economist for Malaysia, Apurva Sanghi, identified a potential reversal in the global AI boom as a key downside risk to Malaysia's economic outlook, Bernama reported.

Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said Malaysia would be significantly exposed to a global slowdown in AI-related activity, given the strong links between its export performance and the electronics, semiconductor and other AI-related supply chains.

Citing World Bank data showing that more than 70 per cent of Malaysia's export growth in early 2026 was attributed to AI-related products, he said a sharp decline in global AI investment could weigh on exports, manufacturing activity, investment and business sentiment.
"However, I would not describe this as an economy-wide vulnerability because Malaysia also has strong domestic consumption, services, energy, commodities and other manufacturing activities.
"The key issue is concentration: if AI-related demand weakens sharply, Malaysia would need other sources of growth to compensate for the external shock," Idham said.
He said Malaysia's semiconductor and E&E exports remained strong, but the country should watch whether demand for semiconductors, servers and data centre equipment starts to slow steadily.

"Other important indicators include semiconductor export growth, global data-centre capital expenditure, new data-centre projects, chip inventories, semiconductor utilisation rates and corporate investment plans by major technology companies.
"A sustained decline across several of these indicators would provide a stronger signal that the AI investment cycle is moderating," he added.
Najib said the bigger risk would be an overreliance on sustained foreign AI investment without building up the country's own technological capabilities.

"This is also where education becomes an economic resilience strategy. If Malaysian workers and companies can apply AI across industries, the benefits of AI become embedded in domestic productivity rather than depending primarily on foreign investment," he said.
DIVERSIFICATION CAN CUSHION SLOWDOWN.
Both economists said Malaysia has several sectors that could help cushion the economy if AI-related activity slows.
This includes infrastructure investment, services, tourism, domestic consumption, energy, commodities, construction, healthcare, logistics and broader manufacturing.

"Malaysia nevertheless has some protection because its economy is relatively diversified. Domestic consumption, services, tourism and infrastructure investment provide alternative growth engines," Najib said.
Idham said services were particularly important, as they were supported by domestic demand and were less directly dependent on the global technology investment cycle.
He said Malaysia could also strengthen tourism, halal industries, healthcare services, food processing, green industries and advanced manufacturing as additional growth engines.
"More importantly, we should use the current AI-driven investment cycle to strengthen the wider economy by developing local suppliers, skills, digital capabilities and higher-value manufacturing.
"That way, even if the AI cycle eventually normalises, the investment and productivity gains generated today can continue contributing to Malaysia's longer-term growth," Idham said.

Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang) will ask the Finance Minister about the demarcation of jurisdiction between the Securities Commission Malaysia and other regulatory agencies to prevent overlapping functions and enforcement.

Tan Hong Pin (PH-Bakri) will also ask the Digital Minister to provide an update on the ministry's achievements in strengthening digital literacy and artificial intelligence (AI) skills, as well as its strategic action plan to develop highly skilled digital talent.

7f3d028b4ead1f93: KUALA LUMPUR: Changes in the implementation method, the Covid-19 pandemic, land acquisition and utility relocation issues, as well as contractor performance have contributed to delays in the Phase 1 Sabah Pan Borneo Highway (LPB) project.

Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the termination of the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019 also required a new procurement process before 15 Phase 1A contractors were awarded the packages in 2021.
"The project delays were caused, among others, by the change in the implementation method from the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model to the conventional method.
"The termination of the PDP model in 2019 also necessitated a new procurement process before 15 Phase 1A contractors were awarded the packages in 2021," he said in a Facebook post.
He said the 2026 Auditor-General's Report had identified 13 findings involving project delays, cost increases, weaknesses in planning and non-compliance with regulations and guidelines.
As of Aug 25, only four of the 35 work packages under Phase 1 had been completed, while the remaining 31 were still under implementation.
Nanta said physical progress stood at 89.01 per cent for Phase 1A, 37.58 per cent for WP09 and 23.96 per cent for Phase 1B.
He said the cost increase for Phase 1A was due to the extension of the project period, changes in scope, construction contract prices, as well as unresolved land and utility issues.
However, he said current site readiness had reached 99.79 per cent for Phase 1A, 96.8 per cent for WP09 and 79.43 per cent for Phase 1B.

He said the Works Ministry had also directed relevant officers in the Sabah Public Works Department and the ministry to attend administration and contract management courses with the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) and the Public Works Department's Centre for Excellence in Engineering and Technology (CREaTE).
The training was aimed at strengthening their skills in preparing Bills of Quantities, cost determination and contract documentation.
In addition, he said the Sabah LPB Steering Committee, established in November 2024, had continued to strengthen monitoring through its site visit programme.

He said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor had also recommended that the committee be co-chaired by the Works Ministry secretary-general and the Sabah state secretary to enhance coordination among state agencies.
80811e70e41a9145: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian consumers face rising egg prices over the next three to six months, with supply constraints, weather disruptions and farm shutdowns driving a sharp market turnaround after years of surplus.

Grade C egg prices, which dipped to around 20 sen in April and May, recovered to roughly 33 sen by the end of June and surpassed 40 sen in August, lifted by Perak farm closures and rising feed costs, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) analyst Jonathan Ooi said.

QL Resources Bhd, one of Malaysia's largest integrated poultry players, expects the uptrend to persist, though margins face pressure. Corn and soybean meal costs are already over 10 per cent higher year-to-date, with cheaper inventory providing only a roughly two-month buffer, Ooi said.

"Management expects egg prices to further increase over the next three to six months but remains cautious as the same feed inflation pressures QL's own cost base, with corn and soybean meal already more than 10 per cent higher year-to-date and cheaper inventory providing a two-month buffer on our estimation," he said.

El Nino conditions are adding modest headwinds, Ooi said, adding that heat stress is lowering layer hen productivity, particularly at open-air farms, with QL describing its impact as neutral to slightly negative.
Strategically, the group aims to grow branded eggs to 25 per cent of egg revenue within five years, from about 18 per cent currently.

Ooi said the retail premium is significant. Branded trays at Jaya Grocer fetch roughly 80 sen per egg versus 40 sen for standard unbranded equivalents, though QL's actual producer-level margin is narrower after accounting for retailer markups, packaging, and enhanced feed for omega-3 varieties.

"Management indicated that its Malaysia operations will focus on efficiency and mix, while Indonesia and Vietnam carry the capacity-growth runway, and Vietnam's losses are expected to narrow as egg prices recover," Ooi said.

Notably, El Niño works in QL's favour elsewhere. Its Marine Products Manufacturing (MPM) division saw revenue rise 18.2 per cent year-on-year and pre-tax profit surge 51.5 per cent, driven by a tighter global fishmeal supply linked to Peru's reduced anchovy catch.

Ooi expects the next two quarters to mark the peak of the current cycle, supported by seasonally stronger fish landings. The key indicator will be Peru's second fishing season in November, which should determine whether the supply squeeze extends into FY28 or begins to ease.
Public Investment Bhd (PublicInvest) onfirms similar recovery signals at Teo Seng Capital.

The firm said recent discussions with the management indicated that egg prices are beginning to recover as excess supply gradually moves back towards equilibrium following the full removal of the government egg subsidy.
"We met with management recently and gathered that there are early signs of egg price recovery, as the oversupply situation gradually returns to equilibrium post subsidy removal," it said.

"Supply tightening is driven by the exit of layer farms that were not able to convert from open-air to closed-house systems. Hot temperatures and air pollution from the haze have adversely impacted egg size and volume," the firm said in a note recently. "The research house said in a note recently.
PublicInvest said birds exposed to higher pollution levels could experience poorer respiratory health, weaker immunity and lower egg production, further tightening supply.

"We expect egg supply in the coming quarter to be lower, with a higher proportion of smaller-sized eggs, providing some near-term price support, though the magnitude and duration remain uncertain," the firm said.
The developments are significant for an industry that has swung sharply between oversupply and shortage.

PublicInvest said Malaysia's egg market has historically experienced sharp cycles. During the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020, an oversupply drove farm-gate prices down by 38 per cent. The market swung into shortage in 2022 before returning to oversupply by 2026.
The imbalance became particularly pronounced after the subsidy was removed in August 2025.
National egg production reached about 16.7 billion eggs, compared with annual consumption of only around 11.6 billion, leaving producers with a substantial supply surplus.
The removal of the subsidy exposed the underlying weakness in the market, with producers unable to sustain previous production levels amid depressed prices and rising operating costs.
The resulting oversupply pushed producers into a prolonged period of weak prices and depressed margins.
Teo Seng's 2QFY26 results reflected the pressure, with revenue remaining broadly flat year-on-year at RM171.4 million as lower sales volume was offset by stable average selling prices.

Core profit after tax and minority interest, however, plunged 83.5 per cent to RM6.9 million after the full removal of the egg subsidy, while its core net profit margin fell 20.6 percentage points to 4 per cent.
PublicInvest now sees the industry moving into a gradual recovery phase, supported by farm exits, lower production and relatively inelastic egg demand.

"We believe the early signs of egg price recovery are encouraging, supported by supply tightening from farm exits and adverse weather conditions, while inelastic egg demand provides a degree of earnings floor," the firm said.

7cf7e7ed22942df1: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Malls remains cautious about global and domestic headwinds, including unresolved trade tensions, prolonged price volatility and rising costs, which could continue to weigh on business and consumer confidence.

Its group managing director H.C. Chan said cost pressures and intensifying competition from both physical malls and e-commerce platforms would continue to put pressure on margins and profitability across the retail industry.

"While our foundation is strong, we remain fully cognisant of global and local headwinds. The unresolved Straits of Hormuz closure will continue to come at a cost for the rest of the world. Higher and prolonged volatile prices are expected.

On the broader national front, Chan said cost pressures and an influx of competition from both physical malls and the online e-commerce platform will continue to exert heavy pressure across the industry.
"These cross currents will weigh heavily on margins and profitability. Yet, our long-term outlook remains resolutely optimistic," he said.
Despite these setbacks, Chan said Sunway Malls remained optimistic about its long-term prospects and was set to expand its portfolio to 16 malls over the next three years.

Chan said Sunway Malls' growth over the past 29 years has been underpinned by three key drivers - close relationships with business partners, an ability to respond swiftly to changing market dynamics, and a relentless focus on innovation.
"These core drivers have enabled us to consistently deliver strong performance and maintain our market leadership position," he said.

In the first half of 2026, Sunway Malls recorded 5.0 per cent year-on-year growth, outperforming the 3.1 per cent industry growth reported by the Malaysia Retailers Association (MRA) and Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA).

7406a8bba7917542: Susulan penyingkirannya yang penuh kekacauan daripada PKR, siri kecaman terdesak dan berterusan Rafizi Ramli terhadap Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim serta pentadbiran kerajaan kini hanya disambut dengan sepi—satu tindakan sengaja oleh kelompok dalaman politik bagi menyekat ruang untuk beliau kembali relevan.

Sejak dipinggirkan, beliau cuba membina semula imejnya sebagai tokoh pembangkang yang lantang, melancarkan kritikan hebat terhadap pentadbiran Madani dari pinggiran politik.

Bagaimanapun, sikap penentangan yang mendadak ini jelas berbaur oportunisme politik. Sebagai arkitek utama strategi ekonomi awal kerajaan terdahulu, Rafizi adalah individu yang memperjuang, merangka, dan mempertahankan kerangka kerja sama yang kini gigih dikritiknya semula.

Kini, selepas memutuskan hubungan sepenuhnya dengan PKR, Rafizi bersama baki pengikutnya beralih ke wadah baharu yang rapuh, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama), dengan harapan dapat menjadi pengacau dalam pilihan raya akan datang.

Namun, percubaan untuk berlakon sebagai penyelamat populis ini mengabaikan realiti yang nyata: modal politiknya sudah hampir muflis, manakala kemarahan rakyat telah merosakkan jenama reformisnya secara kekal.
Gelombang kebangkitan kekecewaan pengundi
Kelemahan ketara jenama Rafizi selama ini adalah ketidakpijakan 'formula' ekonomi yang dicanangnya, yang akhirnya runtuh apabila berdepan realiti tadbir urus eksekutif.

Bagi rakyat Malaysia yang sedang bergelut dengan inflasi struktur, Rafizi berubah daripada seorang juara kelas pekerja yang pernah disanjung kepada simbol kebebalan golongan elit terhadap kesusahan rakyat.

Kemarahan masyarakat ini paling meruncing semasa pelaksanaan rasionalisasi subsidi diesel yang memakan diri. Gaya komunikasi beliau yang defensif dan angkuh ketika krisis itu bukan sekadar menjauhkan sokongan pengundi, malah menyemarakkan kemarahan mereka.

Di saat pedagang tempatan, pengusaha logistik, dan rakyat biasa tenggelam dalam lonjakan kos sara hidup, Rafizi memilih untuk mengajar rakyat daripada kedudukan intelektualnya yang tinggi berbanding menawarkan jaringan keselamatan yang praktikal.
Gelombang kekecewaan pengundi yang amat besar ini telah memberi talian hayat mudah kepada pihak lawan, menjejaskan kedudukan kerajaan sehingga membawa kepada kekalahan teruk pada PRK Sungai Bakap.

Sinisme mendalam dalam kalangan rakyat ini diperkukuhkan lagi oleh penolakan besar-besaran terhadap Pangkalan Data Utama (PADU). Diilhamkan oleh Rafizi sebagai matriks revolusioner untuk bantuan bersasar, PADU sebaliknya bertukar menjadi monumen kegagalan struktur dan punca kemarahan nasional.

Rakyat menyambut projek penanda aras beliau ini dengan penuh curiga sehinggakan kadar pendaftaran menjadi amat hambar, manakala kerajaan negeri—terutamanya Sarawak—menolak terus pangkalan data tersebut atas faktor kelemahan keselamatan dan privasi yang ketara.

Rata-rata rakyat melihat PADU bukan sebagai kejayaan kebajikan, sebaliknya sebagai alat pengawasan autoritarian yang belum matang, yang lebih mengutamakan penjimatan fiskal berbanding kesediaan rakyat.
Kuasa kian lenyap di pinggiran politik

Kerap kali model akademik Rafizi gagal apabila berdepan tekanan realiti, sekali gus membazirkan sejumlah besar dana awam dan masa pentadbiran demi kerangka makroekonomi yang gagal menghasilkan kemakmuran yang boleh diukur.

Dalam isu subsidi bahan api, kedegilan beliau untuk menggantikan diskaun pam pukal dengan mekanisme pemindahan tunai langsung yang rumit menerima tentangan hebat daripada pakar logistik dan kewangan, sebelum akhirnya digugurkan demi alternatif pasaran yang lebih stabil.

Selain itu, tempoh perkhidmatannya sebagai menteri mendedahkan had keupayaan struktur dan hubungan interpersonal yang lemah. Di bawah seliaannya, Kementerian Ekonomi berfungsi seperti sebuah badan pemikir yang terasing dan tidak bertaring, malah kekurangan kuasa fiskal seperti yang dimiliki Kementerian Kewangan untuk melaksanakan peralihan struktur yang sebenar.

Lebih memburukkan keadaan, pergeseran terbuka beliau dengan rakan Kabinet dan pimpinan parti menghakis baki pengaruh dalaman yang ada, sekali gus membuktikan reputasinya sebagai seorang yang sukar diramal dan tidak bertolak ansur menjadikannya satu liabiliti operasi.

Walaupun Rafizi mungkin meninggalkan legasi sebagai seorang pembongkar salah laku (whistle-blower) dalam sejarah, proses tadbir urus menuntut usaha pembinaan negara yang teliti, dan bukannya sekadar gangguan yang melulu. Kepimpinan sebenar memerlukan dasar yang boleh dilaksana dan dikembangkan—bukan sekadar hamburan retorik penuh kekecewaan dari pinggiran politik.

Ketika Rafizi cuba menyelamatkan masa depan politiknya melalui Bersama—cuba menarik pengundi reformis dengan doktrin tegar "empat penolakan" termasuk enggan bersekutu dengan blok politik sedia ada—jalan untuk beliau membuat kemunculan semula kelihatan semakin sempit.
Penganalisis politik berpandangan bahawa wadah baharu beliau ini hampir pasti akan menerima nasib yang sama seperti parti-parti serpihan terdahulu yang akhirnya lenyap dalam pilihan raya.
Bagi rakyat Malaysia yang sudah cukup lelah dengan ketidakstabilan ekonomi dan janji-janji manis yang tidak ditunaikan, nilai formula kosong Rafizi kini secara rasminya telah susut.

c167018eca2d36d6: PETALING JAYA: What does a healthy Malaysian diet look like? Is it the nasi lemak many grew up eating, the bowl of noodles after a long day at work, or the quick breakfast grabbed on the way to the office?
And if a favourite food is part of your routine, does eating healthily mean giving it up altogether?
The answer is more nuanced than a list of foods to avoid. Nutrition is influenced by overall dietary patterns: what you eat, how much you eat, how often you eat and how active you are.

Malaysia’s nutrition challenge, therefore, requires coordinated action from multiple stakeholders, including government, industry and communities, supported by strong healthcare and education systems.
For consumers, however, navigating that bigger picture can be easier said than done.

“Consumer empowerment should go beyond providing information. Malaysians need simple and practical science-based nutrition guidance, but they also need a food environment where healthier choices are available, affordable, accessible and easy to make,” said Indrani Thuraisingham, vice-president of the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca).
“We cannot expect consumers to make better choices if the environment around them makes those choices difficult."

Rozanna M Rosly, a clinical dietitian at UM Specialist Centre, said nutrition and health outcomes are influenced by multiple factors, including education, physical activity, affordability, food accessibility and the wider food environment.
"As such, improving population health requires a multi-pronged approach that supports individuals to make healthier choices, rather than relying on any single intervention," she said.

For Indrani, improving nutrition literacy remains an important public health opportunity in Malaysia. "Giving consumers more information is important, but information only becomes useful when people understand what it means and how to apply it in their everyday choices," she explained.
“Nutrition education, therefore, needs to be practical and continuous, and must begin at an early age."

That education also needs to be sustained, reaching consumers through schools, workplaces, healthcare settings, communities and digital platforms, with messages tailored to different needs and literacy levels.
More broadly, the conversation around nutrition should focus on overall eating habits, dietary balance and lifestyle factors that influence long-term health.
“Healthy eating should be considered in the context of the overall dietary pattern rather than focusing on a single nutrient or food in isolation," Rozanna added.

"While limiting excessive intakes of sugar, salt and saturated fat remains important, we also need to consider portion sizes, frequency of consumption, dietary variety and the overall balance and quality of foods consumed over time.”

Different foods can have a place in a balanced diet when considered in context, while recognising the social and cultural role food plays in everyday life. The practical question, then, is not simply “what should I stop eating?” but “how can I build better habits across my whole diet?”
For that to happen, healthier options must exist in the first place.

A healthier food environment is not defined by any single product or policy. It includes clear nutrition information, affordable options, appropriate portion sizes, healthier alternatives, and practical nutrition education to help consumers make informed decisions.

Product reformulation and innovation can help widen consumer choices - including through efforts to reduce nutrients of public health concern, where appropriate, across different food and beverage categories - while maintaining taste, affordability, safety and consumer acceptance.

Clearer nutrition information and different portion options can complement consumer education, while food innovation and processing can continue to play practical roles in food safety, shelf stability, accessibility and affordability.
This is where industry has a role to play - not as the sole answer to Malaysia’s nutrition challenge, but as one part of a larger effort.
“Creating a healthier food environment is a shared responsibility," said Geoff Parker, Asia Pacific regional director for the International Council of Beverages Associations (ICBA).

"The government can provide the policy and public health framework, businesses can contribute through innovation and reformulation, health professionals can translate science into practical advice, and consumers need the information and choices to make informed decisions.”

For consumers, the goal is ultimately empowerment rather than perfection. No single intervention can address Malaysia’s nutrition challenges on its own, which is why the different pieces need to work together: better nutrition literacy, more accessible and affordable choices, continued innovation, preventive health and a food environment that supports informed decisions.
Ultimately, building more balanced and healthier diets is about helping people develop realistic, sustainable habits before unhealthy dietary patterns and inactivity become entrenched.
It is about having the knowledge, choices, access and support to make healthier decisions more often, while ensuring those decisions are achievable for Malaysians from all walks of life.
18f242eb550b4662: From Moaz Nair

Following his messy departure from PKR, Rafizi Ramli’s desperate, persistent snipes at the prime minister and his administration have been met with total silence—a calculated snub by political insiders to starve him of relevance.
Rafizi’s political career suffered a disastrous blow after his decisive defeat in the PKR deputy president election, forcing his humiliating resignation as economy minister.
Since being cast out, he has tried to reinvent himself as a fiery outsider, launching bitter critiques against the Madani administration from the political wilderness.

However, this sudden adversarial posture reeks of political opportunism. As the chief architect of the government's initial economic strategy, Rafizi championed, designed, and defended the exact frameworks he now desperately tears down.

Now, having fully severed ties with PKR, Rafizi and his remnants have migrated to a fragile new vehicle, Bersama, hoping to play spoiler in upcoming elections. Yet, this attempt to play the populist saviour ignores a damning reality: his political capital is almost broke, and public backlash has permanently shattered his reformist brand.
The groundswell of voter resentment

The fatal flaw of the Rafizi brand has always been the sheer impracticality of his hyped economic "formulas", which completely collapsed under the weight of executive governance. For a Malaysian electorate struggling under structural inflation, Rafizi transitioned from a once-celebrated champion of the working class into the ultimate symbol of elite tone-deafness.

Nowhere was this public backlash more toxic than during his disastrous rollout of the diesel subsidy rationalisation. His defensive, arrogant communication style during the crisis did not just alienate voters; it actively enraged them. While local traders, logistics operators, and ordinary citizens drowned in soaring costs, Rafizi chose to lecture the public from an intellectual high horse rather than offer executable safety nets.

This severe groundswell of voter resentment effectively handed his rivals an open goal, devastating the government's standing and resulting in a self-inflicted electoral bloodbath at the Sungai Bakap by-election.
This deep public cynicism was further cemented by the catastrophic pushback against the central database hub (Padu).
Envisioned by Rafizi as a ground-breaking matrix for targeted aid, Padu instead became a monument to structural incompetence and a lightning rod for national outrage.

The public responded to his signature project with widespread suspicion and dismal registration rates, while state governments—most notably Sarawak—outright rejected the database over glaring security and privacy flaws. Instead of a welfare triumph, the public viewed Padu as an authoritarian, half-baked surveillance tool that prioritised fiscal austerity over public readiness.
A spent force in political wilderness

Time and again, Rafizi’s academic models broke under pressure, wasting massive amounts of public funds and administrative hours on macroeconomic frameworks that failed to generate a single ringgit of measurable prosperity. On fuel subsidies, his stubborn insistence on replacing blanket pump discounts with a convoluted direct cash transfer mechanism faced severe pushback from logistics and financial experts, only to be ultimately scrapped for market-stable alternatives.

Furthermore, his ministerial stint exposed profound structural and interpersonal limitations. Under his watch, the economy ministry functioned like an isolated, toothless think-tank, completely lacking the fiscal muscle of the finance ministry to execute real structural shifts.

Worse, his public friction with Cabinet colleagues and party leaders eroded whatever internal leverage he had left, proving that his reputation as an erratic, unyielding rogue rendered him an operational liability.

While Rafizi may retain a legacy as a historical whistle-blower, governance requires the tedious work of nation-building, not merely reckless disruption. True leadership demands scalable, executable policy—not just bitter rhetorical tantrums from the political margins.

As Rafizi attempts to salvage his future through Bersama, trying to peel away reformist voters with a rigid doctrine of "four no's”—including a refusal to align with established political blocs—his path to an unconventional comeback appears increasingly narrow.
Political analysts point out that his new vehicle is almost certainly doomed to replicate the electoral irrelevance of past vanity parties.
For a Malaysian electorate thoroughly exhausted by economic volatility and unfulfilled promises, the currency of Rafizi’s hollow formulas has officially depreciated.

68ed1579bcdae962: COLORADO: Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane before slamming into the southern US coast early on Saturday, bringing heavy rain, storm surges and possible tornadoes across several states, the National Hurricane Centre said.

The storm is expected to pass through areas with significant offshore oil and gas production, along with onshore refining facilities, which could pressure inventories and already-high prices at the pump.

Michael Brennan, director of the NHC, said in a video briefing on Wednesday that Isaias could be a "major" hurricane — Category 3 or higher — when it makes landfall and could have "multiple, life-threatening impacts from storm surge, heavy rainfall flooding and hurricane force winds."

Isaias would be the first hurricane of the season in the Atlantic, according to the NHC, and could tie the record for the latest first Atlantic hurricane with one that hit on Oct 8, 1905. The strong El Nino weather pattern this year has suppressed Atlantic hurricane development by increasing vertical wind shear, which disrupts the formation of strengthening tropical storms.

About 11.2 million barrels of oil production could be lost across the Gulf through the duration of the storm, a marked increase from the 7.1 million barrels impacted by Tropical Storm Bertha in July, according to a model forecast from consulting firm Earth Science Associates.

The NHC expects Isaias to develop into a hurricane by Thursday as it quickly picks up power over the warm Gulf waters before making landfall early on Saturday, most likely somewhere along the Mississippi, Alabama or Florida Panhandle coast. The storm was located about 805km south of the Louisiana coast early on Wednesday.
Isaias could produce isolated rainfall amounts of 25.4cm across parts of the Gulf Coast, stretching from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle, the NHC said in its latest bulletin.
Tornadoes are possible in the rainbands of Isaias across the Florida Panhandle and Alabama from Friday evening through Saturday, with more tornadoes expected further inland as the storm moves north.
The storm could also produce 3 inches or more of rain further inland, with the NHC warning that "flash and urban flooding, along with isolated river flooding, will be possible" across the Southeast.
Isaias is expected to run into strong upper-level winds, known as vertical wind shear, in the final 24 hours before it reaches the northern Gulf Coast, which could weaken the storm.
Still, the NHC says it is "looking more likely that Isaias will be a significant hurricane when it reaches the coast."
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis on Tuesday had already declared a state of emergency for portions of the state. Some officials across the region were urging residents to voluntarily evacuate.

Florida US Senator Rick Scott wrote on social media that he had spoken with President Donald Trump about the storm, and that "the federal government is going to show up for Florida and make sure we have everything needed to prepare, respond, and recover."

The Marine Minerals Administration, which monitors offshore oil and gas operators in the Gulf of Mexico, said on Wednesday that personnel have been evacuated from eight production platforms and two non-dynamically positioned ahead of the storm.

About 25 per cent of current oil production in the Gulf, or 511,619 barrels of oil per day, has been shut in, the agency said, citing operator reports. Just over 350 million cubic feet per day of natural gas production has also been shut in, or about 16.4 per cent of total output from the region.
The companies with the most exposure to the storm include BP, Chevron, Eni, Murphy Oil and Shell.
