fb27c020b1edcd91: WASHINGTON: The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed that international students pay at least US$70,000 in training fees if they want to work in the country, according to a government notice posted online on Wednesday, part of the Trump administration's wider crackdown on foreign visa holders.

Under the proposal, nonimmigrant students with F-1 visas would be required to pay US$70,000 to a certified institution for on-the-job training, known as Optional Practical Training (OPT), and US$30,000 for any additional work training.
DHS said the new rules were meant "to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect US workers".

Under the OPT system, foreign students can engage in work training for up to 20 hours per week while school is in session, as well as for a limited time after graduation, with an additional allowance for those with degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Those who enrol are currently expected to pay around US$500.
"DHS is now setting a fee to ensure employers, students, and institutions are engaging in appropriate activities consistent with admission as an F-1 nonimmigrant," the agency said.
Such training programmes often serve as a bridge for students seeking work under H-1B visas, which the Trump administration has also targeted with increased fees.

For decades, the H-1B programme has allowed young engineers and scientists from across the world, especially India and China, to turn years of study at US universities into high-paying jobs and a path to permanent US residency.
Leading US tech companies have come to rely heavily on these workers to fill skilled positions.

When he was campaigning in 2024, President Donald Trump vowed he would make it easier for foreign students to remain in the country, suggesting they be automatically awarded a Green Card after graduation.
Like similar DHS proposals, the rule change is likely to be met with swift legal challenges.

"This proposed rule isn't going to fare well in the courts, just as the 100k H-1B fee and other restrictionist policies have been struck down," Doug Rand, director of the Talent Mobility Fund, which works to attract foreign STEM professionals, wrote on LinkedIn on Wednesday.
The proposal is subject to 30 days of public comment before it can be finalised.
DHS said it would wait 60 days after finalisation before putting the rule into effect to allow schools, students and employers time to prepare.
b960e860acbef739: KUALA LUMPUR: The works ministry is taking seriously the findings of the 2026 auditor-general’s report on Phase 1 of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project and will use them to strengthen project delivery and the implementation of other federal government development projects.
Works minister Alexander Nanta Linggi said the national audit department findings included project delays, cost increases, weaknesses in planning and non-compliance with regulations and guidelines.

He said as of Aug 25, only four of the 35 work packages under Phase 1 of the Sabah project had been completed. The remaining 31 packages are still under implementation, with physical progress at 89.01% for Phase 1A, 37.58% for WP09 and 23.96% for Phase 1B.

"Project delays were caused, among others, by a change in the implementation method from the project delivery partner (PDP) model to the conventional method, the Covid-19 pandemic, land acquisition issues, utility relocation and contractor performance.
"The termination of the PDP model in 2019 also necessitated a new procurement process before 15 Phase 1A contractors were awarded the packages in 2021," he said in a Facebook post.
Nanta said the cost increase for Phase 1A was due to the extension of the project period, changes in scope, construction contract prices, as well as unresolved land and utility issues.
The current site readiness status has reached 99.79% for Phase 1A, 96.8% for WP09 and 79.43% for Phase 1B.

Nanta said the relevant officers in his ministry and the Sabah public works department (JKR) have also been directed to attend administration and contract management courses with the Construction Industry Development Board Malaysia and JKR Malaysia’s Centre for Excellence in Engineering and Technology to strengthen their skills in preparing bills of quantities, cost determination and contract documents.
He said the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway steering committee, established in November 2024, had also continued to strengthen monitoring through its site visit programme.
He said Sabah chief minister Hajiji Noor had recommended that the committee be co-chaired by the ministry secretary-general and the Sabah state secretary to enhance coordination among state agencies.
62f144ed6eb9f4ea: KYIV: Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones in one of its most "vile strikes" on Wednesday, president Volodymyr Zelensky said, killing at least 28 people, including children, and damaging industrial facilities and energy infrastructure.
Interior minister Ivan Vyhivskyi put the country-wide death toll at 28.
The heaviest losses were in Pryluky in Ukraine's northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile obliterated a five-storey residential building.
Regional Governor Vyacheslav Chaus said 20 people died in the attack, including five children.
On Wednesday evening, prosecutors in the capital Kyiv said falling debris from a drone killed two people in a suburb.
Zelensky said that 100 people had been injured throughout the country.
The president noted that the attacks coincided with Russian president Vladimir Putin's birthday.
"This is the kind of birthday present that Putin gave himself: the killing of children, the killing of people," Zelensky said in his nightly video address.
In earlier online comments, Zelensky said civilians had also been killed in the capital Kyiv and in the central cities of Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the massive attack.
In total, Russia fired 70 missiles at Ukraine overnight - many of them high-velocity ballistic munitions - and dozens of Shahed attack drones, he said.
"The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively. This was one of the most vile strikes."
In Pryluky, an excavator and dozens of rescuers with shovels sifted through rubble at the site where several sections of the apartment block had collapsed.

Emergency workers used ladders to get to the upper floors of what remained of the building, and brought out 15 survivors as they worked their way down through the rubble. Around 55 people were wounded in the town, regional officials said.

"There's a lot of destruction, especially in the town centre," said Danylo Savenko, deputy mayor of Pryluky, who said he had run to an air raid shelter with his wife as soon as he heard the missiles flying.
Big jump in reported drone interceptions

Russia's defence ministry said its forces had carried out a "massive strike" on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones.
Ukraine's air force said it had downed just over 80% of the 46 jet-powered drones launched by Russia - an increase from recent weeks when air defences took down 50% to 60%.
Since the summer, Russia has used increasing numbers of the new high-velocity drones in round-the-clock attacks on Kyiv and other cities, with Ukraine's air defences struggling to cope.
The air force did not explain the jump in the interception rate and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Zelensky said the Russian ballistic missiles remained the major challenge for Ukraine, adding that he and his team were "every day looking for Patriot (missile interception) systems that can and must protect people's lives".
Ukraine received a new €1.2 billion (US$1.34 billion) tranche from the European Union on Wednesday and will channel the funds towards defence needs, prime minister Sergii Koretskyi said.
The US-made Patriot system is the only weapon in Ukraine's arsenal capable of stopping high-velocity ballistic missiles. Global supplies have been drained by the Iran warand the Ukraine conflict.

Russia's defence ministry said its targets included sites where Ukrainian defence company Fire Point manufactures and stores its Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv as well as regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv.

Last week Zelensky said Ukraine had fired its first domestically made ballistic missile in combat, produced by Fire Point. In an interview with Reuters, he said he expected the company to have a longer-range FP-9 missile ready by the autumn. Fire Point has said that weapon will be able to reach Moscow.
People shelter overnight in Kyiv metro
Zelensky said Ukrainian troops hit four targets in Russia over the past 24 hours, including two Russian oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions.
In the Reuters interview, Zelensky said Ukraine would hit Russia's energy assets in response to Moscow's escalating strikes on civilian infrastructure.
Ukrainian officials and military intelligence shared warnings of the upcoming attacks on Wednesday, and many Kyiv residents took shelter in the city's underground metro stations.
Several loud explosions reverberated through the capital during the night.

In the part of Ukraine's southern Kherson region under Russian control, the regional Russia-installed governor said a Ukrainian drone killed two civilians in a car. And Russia-installed officials in Moscow-held parts of eastern Donetsk Region said three people died in Ukrainian attacks.
8002653b124bf268: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the death of a Russian plague laboratory worker did not appear to be linked to a biological weapon.

b5cc89250a8ce007: WASHINGTON: The US homeland security department (DHS) has proposed that international students pay at least US$70,000 in training fees if they want to work in the country, according to a government notice posted online on Wednesday, part of the Trump administration's wider crackdown on foreign visa holders.

Under the proposal, nonimmigrant students with F-1 visas would be required to pay US$70,000 to a certified institution for on-the-job training, known as Optional Practical Training (OPT), and US$30,000 for any additional work training.
DHS said the new rules were meant "to combat fraud, strengthen the integrity of the immigration system, and protect US workers."

Under the OPT system, foreign students can engage in work training for up to 20 hours per week while school is in session, as well as for a limited time after graduation, with an additional allowance for those with degrees in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Those who enroll are currently expected to pay around US$500.
"DHS is now setting a fee to ensure employers, students, and institutions are engaging in appropriate activities consistent with admission as an F-1 nonimmigrant," the agency said.
Such training programmes often serve as a bridge for students seeking work under H-1B visas, which the Trump administration has also targeted with increased fees.

For decades, the H-1B program has allowed young engineers and scientists from across the world, especially India and China, to turn years of study at US universities into high-paying jobs and a path to permanent US residency. Leading US tech companies have come to rely heavily on these workers to fill skilled positions.

When he was campaigning in 2024, president Donald Trump vowed he would make it easier for foreign students to remain in the country, suggesting they be automatically awarded a Green Card after graduation.
Like similar DHS proposals, the rule change is likely to be met with swift legal challenges.

"This proposed rule isn't going to fare well in the courts, just as the 100k H-1B fee and other restrictionist policies have been struck down," Doug Rand, director of the Talent Mobility Fund, which works to attract foreign STEM professionals, wrote on LinkedIn on Wednesday.
The proposal is subject to 30 days of public comment before it can be finalised.
DHS said it would wait 60 days after finalisation before putting the rule into effect to allow schools, students and employers time to prepare.

4fd24aa003b8e54a: PETALING JAYA: PAS digesa menggunakan tempoh menjelang Belanjawan 2027 untuk membentangkan pelan ekonomi negara yang menyeluruh, bukan sekadar mengetengahkan tekanan fiskal yang perlu ditangani Putrajaya.

Mazlan Ali dari Universiti Teknologi Malaysia berkata Ahli Parlimen PAS perlu memainkan peranan lebih tegas dengan meneliti belanjawan serta mengemukakan hujah berasaskan fakta, penyelidikan dan cadangan alternatif.
Katanya, perkara itu lebih penting memandangkan PAS mempunyai blok Ahli Parlimen terbesar daripada satu parti di Dewan Rakyat, selain menjadi suara utama pembangkang.
“Ahli Parlimen PAS mesti menunjukkan kepada rakyat bahawa mereka mampu menawarkan dasar dan pendekatan yang lebih baik daripada kerajaan perpaduan,” katanya kepada FMT.
Mazlan berkata PAS juga boleh mengukuhkan hujahnya dengan mengetengahkan pencapaian di empat negeri SG4, iaitu Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis dan Terengganu.

Menurutnya, PAS boleh menggunakan kesempatan itu untuk menjelaskan kekangan dihadapi kerajaan empat negeri berkenaan dalam bidang yang bergantung pada peruntukan, kelulusan serta dasar pelaburan kerajaan persekutuan.

Beliau mengulas gesaan Ahli Parlimen Bachok Syahir Sulaiman supaya kerajaan menangani tujuh realiti ekonomi dalam Belanjawan 2027, termasuk ruang fiskal yang terhad, tekanan kos sara hidup, kehilangan pekerjaan, gaji rendah, tekanan terhadap perniagaan kecil serta kebergantungan belia kepada pekerjaan gig.

Syahir berkata petunjuk utama ekonomi, termasuk pertumbuhan 6% pada suku kedua, pengukuhan ringgit serta pelaburan diluluskan berjumlah RM218.5 bilion bagi separuh pertama tahun ini, masih belum diterjemahkan kepada taraf hidup lebih baik bagi rakyat biasa.
Bagi Mazlan, kebimbangan itu akan lebih meyakinkan jika PAS turut menjelaskan apa yang akan dilakukan secara berbeza sekiranya mentadbir di peringkat persekutuan.
“Sebagai parti terbesar di Parlimen, PAS sememangnya perlu mempunyai agenda ekonomi yang jelas untuk negara.
“Ini kerana PAS berpotensi membentuk kerajaan pada masa depan,” katanya.
SG4 sebagai kayu ukur
SG4 merangkumi 5.7 juta penduduk di 32 daerah, dengan Kedah memberi tumpuan kepada sektor semikonduktor serta elektrik dan elektronik, manakala Terengganu kepada tenaga dan petrokimia.
Kelantan pula berperanan sebagai pintu masuk perdagangan rentas sempadan, sementara Perlis memanfaatkan perdagangan sempadan dan tenaga solar.

Ahli ekonomi Harridon Suffian dari Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School menyifatkan prestasi ekonomi negeri ditadbir PAS sebagai bercampur-campur, dengan pencapaian ketara dalam beberapa bidang tetapi kemajuan yang tidak sekata antara negeri SG4.

Katanya, Terengganu menjadi satu contoh negeri yang mempunyai entiti ekonomi lebih maju menerusi Terengganu Incorporated, yang telah mempelbagaikan pelaburannya dalam sektor perladangan, penjagaan kesihatan, hartanah dan hospitaliti.

Sementara itu, anak syarikatnya, Eastern Pacific Industrial Corporation Bhd, telah membina kedudukan dalam sektor minyak dan gas serta perkhidmatan marin, dengan mencatatkan hasil RM411.9 juta tahun lalu.
Kedah juga mempunyai potensi besar menerusi Kulim Hi-Tech Park yang berjaya menarik pelabur utama seperti Intel, Infineon Technologies dan Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik.
Bagaimanapun, Harridon berkata Kelantan dan Perlis masih memerlukan usaha lebih kukuh untuk menarik pelabur serta mempelbagaikan asas ekonomi masing-masing.
“Setiap negeri ditadbir PAS perlu melaksanakan usaha secara konsisten untuk meningkatkan kerancakan ekonomi SG4 secara keseluruhan.
“Negeri SG4 memerlukan hubungan ekonomi yang lebih kukuh supaya dapat menikmati limpahan pertumbuhan daripada wilayah yang berkembang lebih pesat,” katanya.

Jika berjaya, Harridon berkata model SG4 akan mengukuhkan hujah PAS bahawa parti itu mampu membawa pembangunan lebih saksama, termasuk kepada negeri yang mempunyai sumber lebih terhad atau kurang tarikan kepada pelabur.
Mazlan pula berkata pengaruh PAS, khususnya dalam kalangan pengundi Melayu, memberikan parti itu ruang untuk suaranya didengar dalam isu ekonomi.

Bagaimanapun, katanya, kredibiliti PAS bergantung pada keupayaan parti itu beralih daripada sekadar mengkritik kepada membentangkan pelan ekonomi negara yang boleh dinilai pengundi berdasarkan rekod pentadbirannya di negeri SG4.
02a9e210537099a1: PETALING JAYA: Malaysians may be fairly adaptable when life throws them a curveball, but their finances appear to be a different story. A new global study has found that while Malaysian workers score above average for overall personal resilience, financial resilience remains their weakest area.

According to Zurich Insurance Group’s Global People Resilience Study 2026, conducted with Oxford Research & Development Partners, 39% of Malaysian employees say they do not have a savings buffer to fall back on.
The research surveyed 11,175 working-age adults across 16 countries and examined resilience across five areas: psychological, physical, social, financial and digital.

Malaysian workers recorded a score of 4.26 on Zurich’s personal resilience index, higher than the global average of 4.11 and not far behind the highest country score of 4.38. Some 39% of Malaysian respondents also fell into the study’s “thriving” category, with a resilience score above 4.5.
Nevertheless, money emerged as the clearest weak spot: financial resilience was Malaysia’s lowest-scoring domain despite being one of the strongest contributors to overall resilience.
Apart from those without a savings buffer, confidence that insurance or takaful protection adequately meets people’s needs was among the lowest-rated areas measured.
There is, however, an interesting comparison with the rest of the world. Globally, 49% of workers reported having no savings buffer - meaning Malaysians fared somewhat better on this measure.
Even so, only 51% of respondents worldwide felt confident they could manage financially for a few months without income.

The issue matters because financial resilience is not simply about accumulating wealth. In the study, it refers more broadly to whether people can absorb setbacks such as a sudden loss of income, unexpected expenses or caring responsibilities without their overall ability to cope being badly affected.

Zurich’s research also suggests that this can spill over into working life. Employees with the highest resilience reported good or excellent job performance at twice the rate of those with the lowest resilience, while resilience was found to be 2.5 times more predictive of job performance than income.

The Malaysian results were considerably brighter elsewhere: physical health was the country’s strongest resilience driver and its highest-scoring domain. Only 12% of Malaysian respondents reported poor sleep quality, compared with 17% globally.

Malaysians also showed a strong willingness to adapt and learn. Among the highest-rated individual measures were motivation to acquire new skills and confidence in being able to achieve personal goals.

Digital adaptability stood out, too. Some 37% of Malaysian workers said they use generative artificial intelligence every day, compared with 32% globally. Across the wider study, regular users of generative AI tended to report higher resilience scores.
Age produced another notable divide: Malaysian workers aged 18 to 34 recorded a resilience score of 4.30, compared with 4.07 among those aged 50 and above.

Taken together, the findings paint a somewhat paradoxical picture: Malaysians appear relatively confident, adaptable and willing to learn, but a substantial share remain financially vulnerable when something goes wrong.

For those without much of a cushion, the conventional advice remains to build emergency savings gradually. EPF recommends eventually setting aside about three to six months’ worth of essential expenses, although even a smaller amount can provide some protection against unexpected costs.

But perhaps the bigger takeaway from the Zurich findings is that resilience is not only about how well someone copes emotionally or professionally. Sometimes, it can be as simple, and as difficult, as having enough money in reserve when life suddenly changes.
fab9c79912e51f6b: PETALING JAYA: Analysts are urging PAS to use the run-up to Budget 2027 to present a comprehensive national economic plan, rather than merely highlighting the fiscal pressures Putrajaya must address.
Mazlan Ali of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia said PAS MPs should play a more assertive role by scrutinising the budget and presenting arguments based on facts, research and alternative proposals.
He said this was especially important since PAS forms the largest single bloc in the Dewan Rakyat and makes up the dominant voice of the opposition.

“PAS MPs must show the public they can offer policies and approaches that are better than the unity government’s,” he told FMT, adding that the party could strengthen its arguments by pointing to its achievements in the SG4 states of Kedah, Kelantan, Perlis and Terengganu.
Mazlan said PAS could also use the opportunity to outline the constraints faced by the four state governments in areas reliant on federal allocations, approvals and national investment policy.

His comments follow Bachok MP Syahir Sulaiman’s call for the government to address seven economic realities in Budget 2027, including limited fiscal space, cost-of-living pressures, job losses, low wages, pressure on small businesses and youth reliance on gig work.

Syahir said the economic headline indicators — including the 6% growth in the second quarter, a stronger ringgit and RM218.5 billion in approved investments in the first half of this year — have yet to translate into better living standards for ordinary Malaysians.
For Mazlan, such concerns would carry greater weight if PAS articulated what it would do differently at the national level.
“As the largest party in Parliament, PAS certainly needs to have a clear economic agenda for the national economy.
“This is because PAS has the potential to form the government in the future,” he said.
SG4 as test case

The SG4 bloc comprises 5.7 million people across 32 districts, with Kedah focusing on semiconductors and electrical and electronics, Terengganu on energy and petrochemicals, Kelantan serving as a cross-border gateway, and Perlis leveraging border trade and solar energy.

Economist Harridon Suffian of Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School described the economic performance of PAS-led states as mixed, with notable achievements in some areas but uneven progress across the bloc.

Terengganu, he said, offered one example of a more developed state-level economic vehicle through Terengganu Incorporated, which has diversified into plantations, healthcare, property and hospitality.
Meanwhile, its subsidiary, Eastern Pacific Industrial Corporation Bhd, has established a foothold in oil and gas and marine services, recording RM411.9 million in revenue last year.
Kedah also has strong potential through Kulim Hi-Tech Park, which has attracted major investors such as Intel, Infineon Technologies and Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik.
However, Harridon noted that Kelantan and Perlis still need stronger measures to attract investors and broaden their economic base.
“There should be a consistent effort by each PAS-governed state to enhance SG4’s overall economic vibrancy.
“The SG4 states need stronger economic linkages in order to tap into spillover effects from the faster-growing regions,” he said.
If successful, he said, the SG4 model would strengthen PAS’s case that it can deliver more equitable development, including in states with fewer resources or weaker investor appeal.
Mazlan said PAS’s influence, especially among Malay voters, gives it a platform to be heard on economic issues.
However, its credibility, he said, would depend on whether it could move from criticism to a national plan that voters can judge against its SG4 record.
a86a2ca7ed3cf730: SEOUL: Samsung Electronics posted another record profit as surging memory chip prices and relentless spending on artificial-intelligence infrastructure boosted its earnings. The company’s operating profit for the three months through September climbed to about 107.4 trillion won (US$80.1 billion), more than eight times the level a year earlier. Analysts on average had forecast 108.7 trillion won in operating profit. Revenue came to 195 trillion won, lower than expected, preliminary numbers showed Thursday.

The record numbers and elevated expectations underscore how sharply the economics of the AI boom have swung in favour of Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology, as data centre developers race to secure memory chips for their AI servers.

Counterpoint Research raised its forecast for third-quarter DRAM prices to a 10% to 20% sequential increase, from 5% to 10% previously, saying customers are pulling forward orders and gains in pricing power among suppliers.
The boom has transformed Samsung’s semiconductor business, which only a few years ago was grappling with losses after a punishing downturn in demand.

Now, the AI infrastructure buildout is absorbing vast amounts of advanced DRAM, while Samsung is gaining ground on SK Hynix in high-bandwidth memory, the critical chips used alongside Nvidia and other AI accelerators.
The strength of the cycle is also showing up in South Korea’s trade data, with semiconductor exports more than tripling from a year earlier in September.

Analysts on average estimate Samsung’s chip division to post operating profit of 110 trillion won while its electronics unit to report a loss. The Suwon-based company will release a full financial statement around the end of this month.
Investors retain a measure of skepticism around soaring profits in a sector prone to boom-and-bust cycles.
Samsung and SK Hynix are now expanding production capacity while also increasingly backing companies in the AI sector in a bid to drive more demand for their products.
355e4b393c901f4d: UNITED NATIONS: Costa Rica's former vice-president Rebeca Grynspan appeared Wednesday a frontrunner in the race for UN secretary-general as she led informal polling for a fourth time, according to a diplomatic source.
A total of seven candidates -- four women and three men -- are vying to succeed UN chief Antonio Guterres, of Portugal, who ends his second five-year term on Dec 31, 2026.
The selection process is fraught with uncertainty as a single veto from one of the five permanent members of the 15-member UN Security Council can block a potential nominee.
In Wednesday's poll held behind closed doors, Security Council members anonymously assigned each candidate one of three ratings: "encourage," "discourage," or "no opinion".

According to a diplomatic source, Grynspan came out on top with nine "encourage," six "discourage," and zero "no opinion." This is the fourth time she has led the poll out of five rounds held since July.
The veteran diplomat's performance, however, is weaker than in a previous vote on Sept 29, after which she had received only three "discourage," along with 10 "encourage" and two "no opinion."
Argentine Rafael Grossi, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency, came second with six "encourage," seven "discourage" and two "no opinion."
Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, former foreign minister of Guyana, came third.
Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15 available in the Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by the five major powers, which are deeply divided.
Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.
It is tradition that the UN's top job should rotate between different regions. Under that premise, the role should go to a candidate from Latin America this time.

8c78b53131723986: BERLIN: Chancellor Friedrich Merz marked the third anniversary of the Oct 7 Hamas attack on Israel by vowing to fight antisemitism in Germany while pressing for a two-state solution in the Israel-Palestinian conflict.
Antisemitism allegations have become a prominent part of public debate in Germany, involving far-right and far-left parties.

"We are witnessing rising antisemitism in Germany -- antisemitism that far too often goes unchallenged," Merz said, adding that his government "will do everything in its power to resolutely combat antisemitism in all its forms, both new and old".
"Jewish people must be able to live without fear throughout Germany," the chancellor said in the statement marking the anniversary of the Hamas attacks in 2023 that set off the Gaza war.
Merz used the occasion to condemn long-standing political opponents in the far-left Die Linke, who have come under repeated attack over connections to pro-Palestinian activists.
Having defeated Merz's centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU) in Berlin's regional election in September, Die Linke is currently trying to forge a left-wing coalition government.

The chancellor invoked the "horrific terrorist attack" of Oct 7 to argue that the Greens and the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) must shun Die Linke or risk undermining the "non-negotiable principles of our society".

Die Linke maintains that it takes the fight against antisemitism as seriously as the fight against Islamophobia or homophobia, while also emphasising the need to condemn acts by Israel against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
The only plausible political alternative in Berlin to a Die Linke-led government would be a broad centrist coalition that keeps Merz's CDU in power in the capital.
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which has made major inroads in recent state elections, has been accused of ties to neo-Nazi circles.
The Hamas-led attack on Oct 7, 2023, marked the deadliest day in Israel's history, with 1,221 people killed.
Support for Israel

Israel's retaliatory offensive has led to the deaths of more than 74,200 people in Gaza, according to the territory's Hamas controlled health ministry. The UN considers the figures reliable. There have also been clashes between Israeli settlers and Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
Since the attack, German authorities and advocacy groups have reported a sharp rise in antisemitic incidents across the country.
"Germany stands firmly by Israel's side. Our Israeli friends can count on our commitment to ensuring that such a crime never happens again," Merz said.
For decades, Germany has seen resolute support for Israel as a fundamental duty largely because of Nazi Germany's responsibility for the genocide of millions of European Jews during the Holocaust.
But Merz also advocated for the creation of a Palestinian state "alongside Israel" -- something that has been vehemently rejected by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Merz called a two-state solution the best way for "Israelis, Palestinians, and their neighbours to live in peace and security".
Several events commemorating the attack were held across Germany.

On Wednesday evening, several hundred pro-Palestinian demonstrators, including climate activist Greta Thunberg, marched through Berlin wearing keffiyehs and carrying signs denouncing Israeli "genocide" and deploring Germany’s supposed inaction.
Counter-protesters confronted them with Israeli flags and condemned "left-wing antisemitism."
The demonstration was broken up by police, an hour earlier than planned due to several "violations," a statement said.
Jara, an activist who only gave her Christian name, said police confiscated her placard.
It read: "Human beings have the right to exist, not states."
ed632c497b1e980b: BUENOS AIRES: Less than 24 hours after calling time on his international career, Lionel Messi said on Wednesday he was already missing wearing the Argentina jersey.
The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, who scored a penalty in Tuesday's 3-0 win over Benin in his Buenos Aires swansong, had described the occasion as the "saddest day of my career."
Messi led Argentina to World Cup glory four years ago but his team came under severe criticism for their aggressive style of play during their run to the final in July, when they lost to Spain.
"Yesterday was my last match and I'm already missing the light blue and white jersey," said Messi on social media.
But he added: "I know I'm taking the right decision."
Messi is Argentina's record goalscorer with 126 goals, more than double the next most prolific national team player.
He has won a record number of caps with 208, and his 70 assists for the national team are also the best ever.
"It was an incredible journey, full of joy but also some sorrow," he added, while thanking his family and teammates, and paying tribute to Argentina's other football legend, the late Diego Maradona.
c6a0b7485e39ba46: PARIS: Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has become the first person to announce he intends to run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election next year.
The 55-year-old former Switzerland centre-back has been working in finance since he retired in 2004.
It is not the first time, though, that Vega has announced his intention to run for the top job at world football's governing body.
He had considered running against Infantino following the resignation of Sepp Blatter in the wake of a corruption scandal in 2015.
And he tried to challenge his fellow Swiss in 2022, but failed to garner sufficient support to make it onto the ballot.
"The situation has evolved a lot since then," Vega told AFP, adding FIFA's member associations were "much more open to change" than when he previously sought to stand.
"I am standing because my life has prepared me to serve the game," Vega added in an 11-page dossier announcing his candidacy.
"I believe I have a duty and a social responsibility to protect and defend football – its integrity, its people and its future."

Pressure has been building on Infantino, who has lost the support of numerous FIFA member associations, since his aborted plan to create a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA's biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
Last week, the Swiss Football Association became the latest to withdraw its support for Infantino, citing concerns over his record on transparency, accountability and institutional responsibility.
"Faith and trust across the football family have been deeply damaged," said Vega in his dossier.
"We must rebuild both, restore FIFA's credibility and reunite the global football family."
It is not clear whether Vega would be able to stand.
He must first gain the backing of at least five of FIFA's 211 member federations, but also be proposed by one of those.
And the rules stipulate a candidate must have been involved in football for two of the previous five years, and pass an eligibility review.
Potential candidates have until November 18 to meet those criteria.
d8df6fa9b291e5e8: BRUSSELS: Ballooning EU debt could blow a hole in the bloc's next seven-year budget if governments fail to agree on new sources of revenue, auditors warned Thursday.
European Union capitals are locked in the usual battle between so-called "frugal" nations including Germany and higher-spending countries like France.

European leaders will discuss the 2028-2034 budget next week after Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency, presents the latest proposal Saturday that so-called "frugals" say must contain more cuts.
The EU executive proposed a budget worth around two-trillion-euros last year, including plans to raise money from new taxes on large companies, environmental taxation and levies on tobacco.
The European Court of Auditors (ECA) warned the EU economy is facing mounting pressure over the hundreds of billions of euros borrowed to support households and businesses during the covid pandemic.
The EU's debt has "more than tripled in only a few years", reaching €739 billion by the end of 2025, Pierre Moscovici, a member of the European Court of Auditors, told reporters.
The auditors in the report warned: "The EU's rising debt burden could weigh heavily on future budgets. EU borrowing could reach one trillion euros by 2027, largely due to" the covid recovery funds.
They said the EU would be spending up to €93 billion on interest payments alone because of the debt.
The ECA also pointed out the European Commission proposal would allow more new borrowing, for example to support Ukraine or in the event of a major crisis.

"The auditors therefore urge caution in respect of future budgets: without an agreement on new sources of revenue, the EU budget could face a significant shortfall, forcing difficult choices such as higher national contributions and lower ambitions," the Luxembourg-based body said.

Under the Commission proposal the EU would start paying back the covid debt but the European Parliament demands the debt be rolled over. EU lawmakers also want to raise new money through taxes on digital giants and online gambling.
The EU parliament will negotiate on the budget with member states, which usually have the final say over the budget.
Brussels wants leaders to strike a deal by Christmas before several critical elections in Europe, especially the French presidential vote.
EU officials knew that was always optimistic but it appears even more difficult after Spain announced snap elections on Nov 29.

25bd27ae23d078a3: KUALA LUMPUR: The Melaka election can serve as a testing ground for Barisan Nasional's electoral strength and cooperation strategies ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16), said political analysts.

They said BN would have to weigh the opportunity to measure the support it commands against the benefits of a pact, with the implications extending beyond Melaka to its bargaining position ahead of GE16.
Universiti Teknologi Mara political analyst Dr Shafezah Abdul Wahab said BN, particularly Umno, had reason to test its strength by contesting more seats alone.
"Melaka can give BN a clearer indication of its actual support base without relying too heavily on electoral partners," she told the New Straits Times.
However, she did not rule out strategic cooperation in closely contested seats, saying BN would have to balance the opportunity to assess its support against electoral risks.
"For BN, a more solo approach can provide a clearer test of its electoral strength ahead of GE16.
"But there is also a risk of vote splitting, especially in marginal constituencies."
Shafezah said seat allocation remained the biggest challenge, as parties sought to defend the seats they won previously while expanding their presence.
Any agreement would also need grassroots acceptance, she added.
"An agreement between party leaders does not automatically mean supporters and local machinery will accept it.
"Each party has its own candidates, local networks and political calculations."
Cooperation options remain open, with BN having explored possible partnerships and Pakatan Harapan having held discussions with Bersatu, although electoral arrangements have yet to be finalised.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Melaka could test whether parties were moving towards lasting alliances or would continue negotiating separately for each election.

He said a fragmented contest would show that federal-level electoral cooperation did not automatically translate into state-level pacts, adding that it also reflected parties' efforts to preserve their positions ahead of GE16.
"It also suggests that parties are still trying to protect their identities and bargaining positions ahead of GE16, rather than committing themselves too early to permanent alliances."
Tawfik said there was still room to cement a cooperation before nomination day, although this need not involve a grand coalition and could instead take the form of electoral understandings.
"It can involve arrangements for (some seats), avoiding clashes in selected constituencies or allowing certain parties to contest under a common logo."

He said dividing up the state's 28 seats would be difficult, with each party seeking enough constituencies to justify cooperation to its supporters, alongside differences over candidates, logos and preferred partners.
"Cooperation that may make electoral sense mathematically may still be difficult to explain to supporters who have regarded one another as political opponents for many years."

e43bb04ff0100d41: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia’s minimum wage is once again under the spotlight, with workers pushing for higher pay while employers warn against a steep increase as the federal government weighs its options ahead of Budget 2027.
The minimum wage is the statutory floor for basic pay that an employer must pay a covered worker — it does not include allowances, incentives or other additional payments.
But before getting into the arguments being made today, here is a quick look at how Malaysia’s minimum wage has changed over the years.
When did Malaysia introduce the minimum wage?
Malaysia’s minimum wage currently stands at RM1,700 a month.
But did you know it was not always at this level?
In fact, Malaysia first introduced a statutory minimum wage through the Minimum Wage Order (MWO) 2012, which took effect in January 2013, setting the country on a path of periodic wage increases.
The rate was initially set at RM900 a month in Peninsular Malaysia and RM800 in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan.
The MWO was then amended in April 2016, raising the rate to RM1,000 a month in Peninsular Malaysia and RM920 in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan, effective July that year.
It was amended again in 2018, when the government introduced a single nationwide rate of RM1,100 starting in January 2019, effectively removing the regional difference.

The MWO was amended for a third time in December 2019, when the government set the minimum wage at RM1,200 for urban areas and RM1,100 for rural areas, based on the locality of the relevant local authority, effective February 2020.
In April 2022, an amendment to the existing MWO was made and the government introduced a single nationwide minimum wage of RM1,500, which took effect in January 2023.
The most recent increase came in December 2024, when the government introduced the current minimum wage of RM1,700, which took effect in February 2025.
So where does the debate stand?
The next question, then, is when the minimum wage is due for review.
Under Section 25(1) of the National Wages Consultative Council Act, the Council is required to review the minimum wage order at least once every two years.
With the current RM1,700 rate having taken effect in 2025, the minimum wage is due for review by 2027.
Nevertheless, in August, the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) proposed raising the national minimum wage to RM3,100, describing it as a necessary “living wage” benchmark.
MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor was quoted as saying the amount should be considered to reflect the rising costs of food, housing, transportation and other necessities.

He also called for expanding the wage structure to cover middle-income workers whose salaries have remained stagnant at the minimum rate, with some still earning RM1,700 despite a decade of service due to the lack of a defined salary progression framework.

In response, both the SME Association of Malaysia and Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) called on the government to defer any minimum wage increase for now, citing challenging operating conditions.

They cautioned that a blanket increase could severely strain SMEs already grappling with economic headwinds, saying they were not opposed to better wages but stressed that structural support was needed to help businesses absorb higher labour costs.

As for the government, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said in August that the National Wages Consultative Council would review the current minimum wage to decide whether to maintain or raise the rate.
However, by September, Ramanan said no decision had yet been made on a new minimum wage rate, adding that any announcement would only follow Cabinet approval.

With Budget 2027 set to be tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the Dewan Rakyat on October 9, attention is now turning to whether the government will announce any changes to the current RM1,700 minimum wage.
0a600218c49e48f8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Muar MP Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman is officially on the countdown to ending his bachelorhood, with only days remaining before he ties the knot with singer-actress Bella Astillah.

This comes after nearly a year of keeping their relationship under wraps through coy denials and subtle social media posts which culminated in a surprise proposal on top of Mount Kinabalu followed by an engagement on March 28 this year.

As their big day inched closer, more details about their relationship and their wedding have begun to emerge, especially following the premiere of the first episode of the Walimatul Urus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq documentary on Tuesday.
The couple has been affectionately dubbed “BASS” by fans, a portmanteau formed from their initials — the “B” and “A” from Bella Astillah, and the “S” and “S” from Syed Saddiq.
The nickname has since become the couple’s unofficial brand, appearing in the title of their documentary and in the hashtags used across their social media updates.

From customised songket and solemnisation on the 118th floor to kursus kahwin (marriage course) at Four Seasons and more — here’s everything we know so far about Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq’s upcoming wedding.
Multiple receptions and ‘kenduri rakyat’

The pair will then hold a special reception dinner on October 18, set to take place at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) in KL. Both the wedding ceremony and dinner reception will be broadcast live exclusively on Astro.

This is then followed by another wedding reception at Syed Saddiq’s constituency in Muar on October 25 which he described as a ‘kenduri rakyat’ (the people’s feast), where the couple will collaborate with local brands to distribute over RM300,000 worth of daily essentials to families in need.
BASS will then continue the celebrations at Bella’s home state of Sabah where they will hold another ‘kenduri rakyat’ on October 31 at Kota Kinabalu.
Although Bella is from Sandakan, the decision to hold it at Kota Kinabalu was mainly due to logistical reasons.
For now, honeymoon plans remain on the back burner.
Their October 10 ceremony lands right on the heels of the Budget 2027 presentation, leaving Syed Saddiq to head back to Parliament just days later for the policy debate stage.
BASS preparations
Amongst the highlights from their newly released documentary was indeed the wedding preparations.
For their receptions, Bella ordered custom-made handwoven songket from Terengganu Songket, which was founded by the late national master crafter Hajah Zainab @ Ngah Mamat.
She also brought in Faizul Surani, group CEO of Rizalman Ibrahim Group of Companies, as her fashion advisor.
Faizul said that he visualised something classic that was not too typical and held special meaning for the pair and that Bella was very hands-on when it came to their wedding outfits.
“Bella isn’t clueless when it comes to fashion — she knows exactly what she wants and is very hands-on with her wedding plans.
“There were times when she’d ask for a specific thread, and I’d point out that it didn’t look custom-made enough and felt like something easily available off the rack.
“So, we collaborated by blending my ideas with hers to create something truly unique and distinct,” Faizul said in the documentary.

Meanwhile, Terengganu Songket director, Hajar Ariffin said that she was surprised and honoured after learning that Bella wanted to use their service for their special day and she pointed out that the songket ordered by Bella will come directly from Terengganu.

“My mom just flew back to Terengganu to oversee the whole production due to limited time and also because the order is something that is quite complex, intricate and very detailed, so my mom has to be there.
“Hopefully when people see the pair wearing it, it will inspire the younger generation to continue championing and preserving songket heritage,” she said.
Aside from that, their ‘kursus kahwin’ (wedding course), which is mandatory for any Muslim couple, was sponsored by Renaissance KL and Four Points KLCC who also provided them with all-day meals.
In one of the clips from their kursus kahwin, Syed Saddiq, who is a known debater, was also seen debating with the ustaz during one of their classes.

Syed Saddiq along with his supporters and family as well as Bella Astillah as they arrived at the Palace of Justice for his court proceeding in July this year. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Syed Saddiq’s trials

The documentary also shed light on Syed Saddiq’s appeal proceedings following his November 2023 High Court conviction on charges of criminal breach of trust, misappropriation of property and money laundering.

The former youth and sports minister was cleared of all charges following a June 2025 Court of Appeal acquittal and its final reaffirmation by the Federal Court in July 2026 — both hearings were attended by Bella, who at the time was still tiptoeing around their relationship status.
Syed Saddiq revealed in the documentary that his ongoing court case at the time was the thing that held him back from going all in with Bella as he didn’t want to burden Bella and her family.

Meanwhile, in the ‘Dugaan Syed Saddiq’ (Syed Saddiq’s Trials) segment, Syed Saddiq’s father, Syed Abdul Rahman said that he was amazed by his youngest son’s composed nature throughout the whole trial.
“Saddiq truly is extraordinary. He kept his cool throughout.
“I was the one who was freaking out but he never showed any signs of nervousness, instead, he was the one who calmed me down,” Syed Abdul Rahman said.

Meanwhile, Bella’s mother, Siti Zarina Astillah shared that Bella would clear up her calendar and cancel her performances and shows so she could attend Syed Saddiq’s court proceedings to show her support.

Although the couple never publicly disclosed their relationship until after their proposal and engagement this year, Syed Saddiq’s mother, Sharifah Mahani Syed Abdul Aziz, said that Syed Saddiq’s final appearance at court in July was the moment she truly accepted Bella into the family.
She said that the tearful hug that she shared with Bella at the time marked the turning point.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Syed Saddiq’s mother Sharifah Mahani Syed Abdul Aziz said the hug she shared with Bella at The Palace of Justice was the moment she truly accepted Bella into their family. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Syed Saddiq and Bella Astillah’s relationship

The documentary also offers an intimate look into their bond, forged at a time when both were navigating major life turbulence — Syed Saddiq amid his high-profile legal battles, and Bella following her second divorce from Singaporean singer-actor Aliff Aziz in 2024.
Several of Bella’s close friends and family members were featured in the documentary saying that the mother of two was emotionally broken and Syed Saddiq became her light at the end of the tunnel.
Syed Saddiq’s mother and brother said that since he entered the relationship with Bella, he has become more relaxed and easy-going instead of his usual serious self.
“His romantic side is wonderful, cute and beautiful,” Syed Saddiq’s elder brother Syed Abdullah said.
“Even I, who was watching them as viewers, was smitten (looking at BASS). I always be like aww, this guy is so sweet,” he said.
“Previously, whenever he spoke, it would always be about facts. But he knows how to make jokes now,” Sharifah Mahani said.

The documentary also touches on the pair’s March 28 engagement, particularly Syed Saddiq’s engagement gift trays (hantaran) which came in the form of an engagement ring, an Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad savings account and a Tabung Haji savings account for Bella as well as a couple of National Education Savings Scheme (SSPN) accounts for Bella’s children Ayden Adrean and Ara Adreanna.

Bella said that she initially felt that the hantaran looks like an ‘aid for single mothers’; however, Syed Saddiq defended his decision, saying that the gifts are proof of his long-term commitment to Bella and her children.
“To me, it’s quite straightforward: I want to make sure both children receive the best possible education.

“I also have to remind myself that I’m not just marrying Bella — I’m marrying her two children as well. I wanted to show them that I’m serious and that this is a long-term commitment, not a short-term plan.
“It was my way of binding us together as a family, rather than just linking Bella and me,” he said.
The over 40-minute documentary also showcased more behind the scenes looks at BASS and their relationship including how they introduced themselves to their families.
The next episode of Walimatul Urus Bella Astillah & Syed Saddiq will be the live broadcast of their October 10 wedding ceremony and October 18 dinner reception.

The solemnisation ceremony of Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq will be broadcast live across Astro Ria (Channel 104), Astro Prima (Channel 105), and Astro Awani (Channel 501), as well as streamed on Sooka and Astro GO.
